semin-durr:77-77.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {سُنَّةَ}: there are three views on it. First: that it is accusative as an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) [mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], i.e. "Allah established that as a sunna (practice)", or "We established that as a sunna". Second — stated by al-Farrāʾ — that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "like the sunna of Allah"; on this view one does not pause at His words «إلا قليلاً». Third: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "follow the sunna".

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِدُلُوكِ}: there are two views on this lām. First: that it means «بَعْد» (after), i.e. "after the declining (دُلوك) of the sun". Similar to it is the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra:
309 - 0- فلمَّا تَفَرَّقْنا كأني ومالِكاً ... لطولِ اجتماعٍ لم نَبِتْ ليلةً معاً
(When we parted, it was as though Mālik and I — after [lām] a long time together — had never spent a single night together.)
And similar to it is their expression «كَتَبَتْه لثلاثٍ خَلَوْنَ» ("I wrote it after three [nights] had passed"). Second: that it has its basic meaning, i.e. "because of the declining". Al-Wāḥidī said: "Because it [the prayer] becomes obligatory only by the sun's passing the meridian."
Al-dulūk is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of دَلَكت الشمسُ, and there are three opinions about it. The best known: that it is the zawāl (the sun's passing the meridian), which is midday. Second: that it is [the period] from the zawāl to sunset. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its derivation is from al-dalk (rubbing), because a person rubs his eye when looking at it [the sun]." I say: this implies that it is not a maṣdar, since he made it derived from the maṣdar. Third: that it is sunset; al-Farrāʾ cited in support of this:
309 - 1- هذا مُقامُ قَدَمَيْ رَباحِ ... ذَبَّبَ حتى دَلَكَتْ بَِرَاحِ
(This is the standing-place of Rabāḥ's two feet; he kept [the herd] moving until Barāḥ declined.)
i.e. Barāḥ set, and that is the sun. Ibn Qutayba cited for this the verse of Dhū al-Rumma:
309 - 2- مصابيحُ ليسَتْ باللواتي تقودها ... نُجومٌ ولا بالآفلاتِ الدوالِكِ
(Lamps that are not of those led by stars, nor of those that vanish and set [الدوالك].)
i.e. the setting ones. Al-Rāghib said: "The dulūk of the sun is its inclining towards setting; it is from their expression دَلَكْتُ الشمسَ: 'I pushed it away with the palm [al-rāḥ]'. From it: دَلَكْتُ الشيءَ في الراحةِ ('I rubbed the thing in the palm'), and دَلَكْتُ الرجلَ: 'I put the man off [in paying a debt]'; al-dalūk: whatever perfume you rub on; and al-dalīk: a food made of butter and dates."
His words: {إلى غَسَقِ اليل}: there are two views on this preposition-phrase. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَقِمْ», so it is for the terminal limit of the establishing [of the prayer]; likewise the lām in «لِدُلوك» is also attached to it. Second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الصلاة», i.e. "establish it extended until the darkness of the night"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. There is reservation about this, in that he assumed the omitted element to be a specific (restricted) being, unless he intends an explanation of the meaning, not of the iʿrāb.
Al-ghasaq is the onset of the beginning of the night; Ibn Shumayl said this, and he cited:
309 - 3- إنَّ هذا الليلَ قد غَسَقا ... واشتكيْتُ الهَمَّ والأرقا
(This night has grown dark [غسق], and I have complained of care and sleeplessness.)
It is also said: it is the blackness of the night and its darkness. Its origin is from flowing: غَسَقَتِ العين, i.e. the eye's tears flowed; it is as though the darkness pours onto the world and flows over them. [The poet] said:
309 - 4- ظلَّتْ تجودُ يداها وهي لاهِيَةٌ ... حتى إذا هَجَمَ الإِظْلامُ والغَسَقُ
(Her two hands kept on giving while she was heedless, until darkness and ghasaq fell suddenly.)
And it is said: غَسَقَتِ العينُ: the eye filled with tears; غَسَقَ الجرحُ: the wound filled with blood; so it is as though darkness filled all existence. As for al-ghāsiq in His words {وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ} [al-Falaq: 3], it is said that what is meant is the moon when it is eclipsed and turns black; and it is said: the night. Al-ghasāq, with and without doubling [of the sīn], is the pus that flows from the people of the Fire. One says غَسَق الليلُ and أَغْسَقَ, ظَلَمَ and أَظْلَمَ, دَجَى and أَدْجَى, غَبَشَ and أَغْبَشَ; al-Farrāʾ transmitted this.
His words: {قُرْآنَ الفجر}: there are several views on it. First: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الصلاة», i.e. "and establish the recitation (qurʾān) of the dawn", what is meant being the morning prayer, expressed by one of its pillars. Second: that it is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "and [hold to] — عليك — the recitation of the dawn"; al-Akhfash gave this implied form and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him. The principles of the Basrans reject this, because verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) do not operate when implied. Third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "make much recitation" or "keep to the recitation of the dawn".

semin-durr:79-79.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمِنَ اليل}: there are two views on this «منْ». First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَهَجَّدْ», i.e. "keep vigil with the Qurʾān for part of the night". Second: that it is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "and rise for a rising from the night", or "and stay awake for part of the night"; al-Ḥawfī mentioned both. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And [hold to] — عليك — part of the night, and keep vigil with it." If he meant an explanation of the meaning, it is close; but if he meant an explanation of the iʿrāb, it is not valid, because the thing incited to (al-mughrā bihi) cannot be a particle; and his making «مِنْ» mean "part" does not require it to be a noun — the proof being that the wāw of «مع» (accompaniment) is not a noun by consensus, even though it means an explicit noun, namely «مع». / The pronoun in «به»: the apparent view is that it refers back to the Qurʾān as such, without restriction to its being annexed to "the dawn". Second: that it refers back to the implied time, i.e. "and rise for a time of the night, and keep vigil in that time", so the bāʾ means «في» (in).
His words «نافِلَةً»: there are several views on it. First: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "you perform a supererogatory act as an extra (nāfila) for yourself beyond the obligatory prayers". Second: that it is accusative by «تَهَجَّدْ», because it carries the meaning of "perform supererogatory prayer", as though it were said: "perform supererogatory prayer as a nāfila". Al-nāfila is a maṣdar like al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. Third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "[as] a prayer of nāfila"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; it would then be a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «به» if you make it refer to the Qurʾān, not to an implied time. Fourth: that it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); this is the apparent sense of al-Ḥawfī's statement, for he said: "«نافلةً» may be accusative by «تهجَّدْ» if you take it in the sense of: pray with it a nāfila, i.e. pray a nāfila for yourself."
Al-tahajjud is abandoning al-hujūd, which is sleep; the form tafaʿʿala comes for privation, as in تَحَرَّجَ and تَأَثَّمَ (to avoid sin), and in the ḥadīth: «كان يَتَحَنَّثُ بغارِ حراءٍ» ("He used to devote himself to worship [lit. avoid sin] in the cave of Ḥirāʾ"). There is disagreement among the lexicographers about al-hujūd. It is said: it is sleep. [The poet] said:
309 - 5- وبَرْكُ هُجودٍ قد أثارَتْ مَخافتي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And many a herd of sleeping [هجود] camels my fearsomeness has roused …)
Another said:
309 - 6- ألا طَرَقَتْنا والرِّفاقُ هُجودُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Lo, she visited us by night while the companions were asleep [هجود] …)
Another said:
309 - 7- ألا زارَتْ وأهلُ مِنَىً هُجودُ ... وليت خيالَها بمِنَىً يعودُ
(Lo, she visited while the people of Minā were asleep [هجود] — would that her phantom might return to Minā.)
So hujūd means sleepers, plural of «هاجِد» like sājid and sujūd. It is also said: al-hujūd is shared between the sleeper and the one praying. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "تَهَجَّدَ: he prayed at night; and تَهَجَّدَ: he slept", and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda and al-Layth.
His words: {عسى أَن يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَاماً}: there are four views on the accusative of «مَقاماً». First: that it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "He will raise you in a station". Second: that it is accusative by the meaning of «يَبْعَثُك», because it carries the meaning of "He will set you up"; one says "he was set up (أُقِيم) from his grave" and "he was raised (بُعِث) from it" with one meaning; so it is like "he sat (قعد) a sitting (جلوساً)". Third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "He will raise you possessing a praised station". Fourth: that it is an emphatic maṣdar whose governing word is implied, i.e. "so you will stand a standing".
On the first three views, but not the fourth, «عَسَى» must be the complete (tāmma) [verb], so it is predicated of «أنْ» and what is within its domain. For if it were the defective (nāqiṣa) one, with {أَن يَبْعَثَكَ} as a fronted khabar (predicate) and «ربُّك» as a postponed noun [of ʿasā], something forbidden would follow: namely separating, by something extraneous, between the ṣila (relative clause) of the [nominal-]relative and what it governs. For «مَقاماً», on the first three views, is accusative by «يَبْعَثُكَ», which is the ṣila of «أَنْ»; so if you make «رَبُّك» the noun of [ʿasā], it is extraneous to the ṣila and may not separate; but if you make it the fāʿil (agent) [of يبعث], it is not extraneous, so separation by it does not matter.
As for the fourth view, it may be the complete or the defective [ʿasā] with fronting and postponing, since nothing forbidden arises, because «مقاماً» is governed by something other than the ṣila. This is among the fine points of the craft of grammar, and you have had something close to it earlier in Sūrat Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, in the words of Allah the Exalted: {أَفِي الله شَكٌّ فَاطِرِ} [Ibrāhīm: 10].

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ}: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), and the latter is the apparent view. The majority read with ḍamma on the mīm in both [مُدخل and مُخرج], because a quadriliteral verb precedes them. Qatāda, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ḥumayd read with fatḥa on the mīm in both: either because they are maṣdars with the augments removed, like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], or because they are accusative by an implied verb corresponding to them, its implied form being "so enter an entering (مَدْخَل) and go out a going out (مَخْرَج)". This was discussed fully earlier under the reading of Nāfiʿ in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, and that he read likewise in Sūrat al-Ḥajj.
«مُدْخَلُ صِدْقٍ» and «مُخْرَجُ صِدْقٍ» are an explanatory annexation (iḍāfat al-tabyīn); according to the Kufans, they are the annexation of the described to its adjective, because it [صدق] is used as an adjective for emphasis.
His words: «سُلْطاناً»: it is the first object of «جَعَل» (making), and the second is one of the two preceding preposition-phrases, while the other is attached to its being-settled (istiqrār). «نصيراً» may be converted from [the pattern] fāʿil for intensiveness, or it may have the meaning of mafʿūl (passive sense).

semin-durr:81-81.t:
Al-zuhūq is going away and vanishing. [The poet] said:
309 - 8- ولقد شَفَى نَفْسي وأبرَأَ سُقْمَها ... إقدامُه بمَزَالَةٍ لم يَزْهَقِ
(What healed my soul and cured its sickness was his advancing in a place of slipping without his perishing [يزهق].)
One says: زَهَقَتْ نَفْسي تَزْهَقُ زُهوقاً, with ḍamma. As for al-zahūq with fatḥa, it is an intensive form, as in his words:
309 - 9- ضَرُوْبٌ بنَصْلِ السَّيْفِ سُوقَ سِمانِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(One who strikes much [ضروب] with the sword's blade the shanks of the fat ones among them …)

semin-durr:82-82.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِنَ القرآن}: there are three views on this «مِنْ». First: that it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins); al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this from them: the [مِن] of clarification must be preceded by what it clarifies, not precede it, whereas here it is found preceding it.
Second: that it is partitive. Al-Ḥawfī rejected this, saying: "Because it would then follow that part of it is not a healing." It was answered that its sending down is what is in parts. This answer is not evident. Abū al-Baqāʾ answered that part of it heals from illness. I say: this has indeed occurred, as proven by one of the Companions' reciting al-Fātiḥa as a ruqya (healing incantation) over the chief of the tribe who had been stung, and he was healed.
Third: that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and this is clear.
The majority read «شِفاءٌ/ ورحمةٌ» nominative, as two khabars (predicates) of «هو», the clause being the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read both accusative, and his reading was explained as their being accusative as ḥāls (circumstantials), the ṣila then being «للمؤمنين», with the ḥāl fronted before its abstract governing element, like His words {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ} [al-Zumar: 67] in the reading of those who make «مَطْوِيَّاتٍ» accusative, and the verse of al-Nābigha:
310 - 0- رَهْطُ ابنِ كُوْزٍ مُحْقِبي أَدراعَهم ... فيهم ورَهْطُ ربيعةَ بنِ حُذارِ
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, carrying their coats of mail behind them [محقبي], are among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
It is also said: both are accusative by an implied verb; this is [the position of] those who forbid fronting it [the ḥāl] before its abstract governing element. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Al-Kisāʾī permitted «ورحمةً» in the accusative, conjoined to «ما»." The apparent sense of this is that al-Kisāʾī left «شفاء» in the nominative and made only «رحمة» accusative, conjoined to the relative «ما», as though it were said: "and We send down of the Qurʾān a mercy"; and there is nothing in his report indicating that he recited it as Qurʾān. The disagreement [over] «وننزل» with or without doubling was given earlier. The majority read with the nūn of majesty; Mujāhid read «ويُنْزِل» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], i.e. Allah.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَنَأَى}: the majority read with the hamza before the weak letter, from al-naʾy, which is distance. Ibn Dhakwān — and the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted it from Ibn ʿĀmir in full — read «ناءَ», with the alif before the hamza. There are two explanations for it. First: that it is from ناء يَنُوْءُ, i.e. "he rose (with effort)". The poet said:
310 - 1- حتى إذا ما التأَمَتْ مَفاصِلُهْ ... وناءَ في شِقِّ الشِّمالِ كاهلُهْ
(Until, when his joints had knit together and his shoulders rose heavily [ناء] on the left side.)
Second: that it is metathesized (maqlūb) from نأى, its pattern being falaʿa, as they say «راءَ» for «رأى», and other such cases; but whenever it is possible to avoid metathesis, that is preferable. This same disagreement also occurs in Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim inclined the alif with full imāla (inclination); al-Sūsī [read it] between the two (bayna bayna), with a disagreement reported from him; likewise in Fuṣṣilat, except Abū Bakr, who did not incline it [there].
Khalaf, Abū al-Ḥārith and al-Dūrī from al-Kisāʾī inclined the fatḥa of the nūn in both sūras.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {على شَاكِلَتِهِ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَعْمل». As for al-shākila, the best that has been said about it is what al-Zamakhsharī said: that it is his way which resembles (yushākilu) his state in guidance and misguidance, from their expression "a road with shawākil", which are the paths that branch off from it; and the proof of this is His words {فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أهدى سَبِيلاً}. It is said: according to his religion; it is said: his character. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "his side". Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the manner and way upon which he was created."
It is from «الشَّكْلِ», which is the like; one says: "you are not of my shakl nor of my shākila". As for «الشِّكْلُ» with kasra, it is the appearance; one says: "a girl of beautiful shikl". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
310 - 2- حَيِّ الحُمولَ بجانب العَزْلِ ... إذ لا يُلائم شَكلُها شَكْلي
(Greet the camel-borne litters beside al-ʿAzl, since her like [شكلها] does not suit my like [شكلي].)
i.e. her like does not suit my like.
[Translator's note: the text says «وأمَّا "الشَّكْلُ" بالكسر», writing the vowel of the first letter as fatḥa while stating "with kasra"; the intended word is الشِّكْل.]
His words: «أَهْدى»: it may be from «اهْتَدى» with the augments removed; or from the transitive «هَدَى»; or from the intransitive «هدى» meaning اهتدى. «سبيلاً» is a tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:85-85.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّن العلم}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أُوْتِيْتُم». It may not be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قليلاً», because if it were placed after it, it would be an adjective; [and it cannot be fronted thus] because what is within the domain of «إلاَّ» does not precede it.
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and al-Aʿmash read «وما أُوْتُوا» ("and they were not given") with the pronoun of the absent [third person].

semin-durr:87-87.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً}: there are two opinions about it. First: that it is a connected exception (muttaṣil), because it is included in His words «وكيلا». Second: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), so it is rendered by «لكن» (but) according to the Basrans and by «بل» (rather) according to the Kufans. «مِنْ ربِّك»: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رحمة», or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of it.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The words of the Exalted: {سُبْحَانَ}: the discussion of it has preceded in full at the beginning of al-Baqara. And «أَسْرى» and «سَرَى» are two dialectal forms; the discussion of them has preceded in Sūrat Hūd, together with the fact that some restricted «أَسْرى» to the night. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: the isrāʾ (night journey) is only by night, so what is the meaning of mentioning the night? I say: by His words «ليلاً», in indefinite form, He intended to make the duration of the night journey small, and that he was taken by night in part of the night from Mecca to Syria, a journey of forty nights; that is because the indefiniteness indicates partiality. The reading of ʿAbd Allāh and Ḥudhayfa, «من الليل» (of the night), i.e. part of it, bears witness to that, as in His words: {وَمِنَ الليل فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 79]." End of quote. So «سَرى» and «أسْرى» are like «سَقَى» and «أَسْقى», and the hamza is not for transitivity; the transitivity is only by the bāʾ in «بعبده». It has preceded in al-Baqara that, according to the majority, it does not entail the agent accompanying the object, contrary to al-Mubarrad.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that the object of «أَسْرى» is omitted and that the transitivity is by the hamza, saying: "It appears that «أَسْرى» is made transitive by the hamza to an omitted object, i.e. He made the angels journey by night with His servant, because it is awkward to ascribe «أسرى», when it is in the sense of «سرى», to Allah the Exalted, since it is an act that entails movement, like walking, running, coming and moving; so it is not good to ascribe any of this [to Him] while there is an alternative to it. If anything of that occurs in the revealed law, we interpret it, as in: 'I come to him running (harwala)'."
I say: all of this he built only on the belief that transitivity by the bāʾ entails the agent's accompanying the object in that; and the rebuttal of this position has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara, on His words {وَلَوْ شَآءَ الله لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ} [the verse: 20]. Then he allowed «أَسْرى» to be in the sense of «سَرَى» with the omission of a muḍāf, as in His words: {ذَهَبَ الله بِنُورِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 17], meaning that the implied form would be: "He whose angels journeyed by night with His servant"; and what led him to that is the belief in accompaniment mentioned above.
His words: «لَيْلاً» is in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the benefit of its indefiniteness has preceded. And «من المسجد» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
His words: «حولَه»: there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is in the accusative as an adverb, and the verification of the discussion of it has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The second: it is an object. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "i.e. We made good and made to grow." He means that He made [بارَكْنا] include the meaning of a verb that is transitive by itself. This is open to question, because it [حول] is not declinable (lā yataṣarraf, i.e. it is used only as an adverb).
His words: «لِنُرِيَه»: the majority read it with the nūn of majesty, in keeping with «بارَكْنا». In them there are two iltifāts (shifts of person): from the third person in His words {الذي أسرى بِعَبْدِهِ} to the first person in «بارَكْنا» and «لِنُرِيَه», then He shifted to the third person in His words «إنه هو», if we refer the pronoun to Allah the Exalted — and that is correct; so in the speech there are two iltifāts.
Al-Ḥasan read «لِيُرِيَه» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. Allah the Exalted; on this reading there are four iltifāts in this verse. That is: He shifted first from the third person in His words {الذي أسرى بِعَبْدِهِ} to the first person in His words «بارَكْنا»; then He shifted secondly from the first person in «بارَكْنا» to the third person in «لِيُرِيَه» on this reading; then He shifted with the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source, «ثم التفت بالياء»; the sequence suggests «ثالثاً», "thirdly"] from this third person to the first person in «آياتنا»; then He shifted fourthly from this first person to the third person in His words «إنه هو», on the correct view of the pronoun, that it is for Allah. But according to a view which Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted, that the pronoun in «إنه هو» is for the Prophet ﷺ, that does not follow, and there is one iltifāt in the reading of the majority and three in the reading of al-Ḥasan. This is a rare passage; the most that iltifāt has occurred [in one place] is three times, according to what al-Zamakhsharī said about the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
302 - 5- تطاوَلَ ليلُكَ بالإِثْمِدِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Long has your night grown at al-Ithmid …)
— the verses. The dispute with him about that, and some of what can be answered to him, has preceded at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa.
And if someone were to claim that there are five iltifāts in it, one would need clear evidence to refute him; the fifth is the iltifāt from «إنَّه هو» to the first person in His words {وَآتَيْنَآ مُوسَى} — the verse.
The seeing (al-ruʾya) here is visual. It is also said: mental; Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, for he said: "It is possible that He means: that We may show Muhammad to people as a sign, i.e. that the Prophet ﷺ should be a sign in that Allah does this with a human being." So the seeing is mental on this view.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَآتَيْنَآ}: there are three views on it. The first: this clause is conjoined to the preceding clause of declaring the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, transcendent; and conjunction of clauses does not require sharing in a predicate or anything else. The second: al-ʿAskarī said: it is conjoined to «أسرى». The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] considered this far-fetched. The reason it is far-fetched is that what is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) is itself a ṣila, so the analysis leads necessarily to the construction: "Glory be to Him who took by night and We gave", which has the force of "Him who We gave Moses", so a first-person pronoun would refer back to the relative noun without any justification for that.
The third: it is conjoined to what is implied in His words «أسرى» of the statement, as though He said: "We took Our servant by night, showed him Our signs and gave"; and this is closer to explaining the meaning than to iʿrāb.
His words: «وجَعَلْناه»: the accusative pronoun may refer back to the Book — and this is the apparent view — or it may refer back to Moses, peace be upon him.
His words: {لِّبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ}: it may be attached to «هدى» itself, as in His words {يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ} [Yūnus: 35]; or it may be attached to the making, i.e. We made it for their sake; or it may be attached to something omitted, as a naʿt (adjective) of «هُدى».
His words: {أَلاَّ تَتَّخِذُواْ}: «أَنْ» may be the one that puts the verb in the accusative, with the omission of the particle of cause, i.e. "so that you do not take". It is also said: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: "out of dislike that you should take". Or it may be the explicative (mufassira) أن with «لا» prohibitive; so the verb is accusative on the first view and jussive on the second. Or, according to some, it may be redundant, the clause after it being governed by an implied verb of saying, i.e. "it being said to them: do not take", or "We said to them: do not take"; and this is apparent in the reading with address. This is rejected on the grounds that it is not one of the places where «أَنْ» is redundant.
Abū ʿAmr read {أَنْ لا يتَّخذوا} with the yāʾ of the third person, in keeping with His words {لبني إسرائيل}, and the rest with address, as an iltifāt (shift of person).

semin-durr:3-3.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذُرِّيَّةَ}: the majority read it in the accusative, and there are several views on it. The first: it is in the accusative by specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī began with this. The second: it is in the accusative as a badal (substitute) of «وَكِيلاً», i.e. "that you not take besides Him the offspring of those We carried". The third: it is in the accusative as a badal of «موسى»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is extremely far-fetched. The fourth: it is in the accusative as the first object of «تتخذوا», the second being «وكيلاً», which was placed first; «وكيلاً» is then one of the words that come singular in wording while plural is meant, i.e. "do not take the offspring of those We carried with Noah as guardians", as in His words: {وَلاَ يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَن تَتَّخِذُواْ الملائكة والنبيين أَرْبَاباً} [Āl ʿImrān: 80].
The fifth: it is in the accusative as a vocative, i.e. "O offspring of those We carried". They restricted this view to the reading with address in «تتَّخذوا», and it is clear on that reading, though it is not required — even though Makkī disallowed it, for he said: "As for whoever read «يتَّخذوا» with the yāʾ, ذرية is an object and nothing else, and the vocative is far-fetched, because the yāʾ is for the third person and the vocative is for address, so they do not come together except far-fetchedly." It is not as he claimed, since a person may address one individual and give information about another, saying: «يا زيدُ ينطلقٌ بكرٌ وفعلتَ كذا» (O Zayd, Bakr is going off, and you did such-and-such) and «يا زيدُ ليفعلْ عمروٌ كيتَ وكيت» (O Zayd, let ʿAmr do such-and-such).
A group read «ذُرِّيَّةُ» in the nominative, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "it is the offspring"; [Abū] al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is not clear. The second: it is a badal of the wāw of «تتَّخذوا». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is not permitted in the reading with the tāʾ, because you do not substitute for a second-person pronoun; if you said «ضربْتُك زيداً» (I struck you, Zayd) as a badal, it would not be permitted."
The Shaykh rebutted him for this unrestricted statement and said: "Distinction is needed: if it is a substitute of the part or of inclusion, it is permitted; and if it is of the whole for the whole and conveys comprehensiveness, as in «جئتُمْ كبيرُكم وصغيركم» (you came, your great and your small), al-Akhfash and the Kufans allowed it." He said: "And that is correct." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's giving the example «ضَرَبْتُكَ زيداً» may protect him from this rebuttal.
Makkī said: "The nominative is permissible in ordinary speech on the reading of whoever read it with the yāʾ, as a badal of the pronoun in «يتَّخذوا»; and that is not good on the reading with the tāʾ, because the third person is not substituted for the addressee. And the genitive is permissible as a badal of بني إسرائيل." I say: as for the nominative, it has preceded that it was read, and it is as though he did not come across it [Translator's note: the source has «ام يَطَّلِعْ», evidently a misprint for «لم يَطَّلِعْ»]. As for the genitive, it has not been read, as far as I know. And there applies to him, regarding his words "because the third person is not substituted for the addressee", what applied to Ibn ʿAṭiyya — indeed more so, because he did not mention an example clarifying what he meant, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya did.
The words of the Exalted: {مَنْ حَمَلْنَا}: [«مَنْ»] may be a relative (mawṣūla) or qualified (mawṣūfa).

semin-durr:88-88.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَ يَأْتُونَ}: there are two views on it. The more evident of them: that it is the answer to the oath prepared for by the lām [the lām al-tawṭiʾa]. Second: that it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); they excused its being in the nominative on the ground that the protasis is past, so it is like his words:
310 - 3- وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حِرِمُ
(And if a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)
They cited in support of it the verse of al-Aʿshā:
310 - 4- لئِنْ مُنِيْتَ بنا عن غِبِّ معركةٍ ... لا تُلْفِنا مِنْ دماءِ القومِ نَنْتَفِلُ
(If you are confronted with us after a battle, you will not find us disowning the blood of the enemy.)
Here he answered the condition despite the preceding lām of preparation (tawṭiʾa); this is evidence for al-Farrāʾ and those who followed him in that, and in it is a refutation of the Basrans, since they make the answer to the oath obligatory when there is no preceding element that has a khabar (predicate).
Some answered that the lām in the verse is not for preparation but redundant (zāʾida); this is nothing/ because there is no evidence for it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Were it not for the preparatory lām, it could be the apodosis of the condition, as in his words:
310 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… he says: neither absent …)
because the protasis occurs as a past [verb]." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed with him: this is not the position of Sībawayh, nor of the Kufans and al-Mubarrad; for Sībawayh's position on such a case is that it is intended to be fronted, and the position of the Kufans and al-Mubarrad is that it is on [the basis of] omission of the fāʾ; this is a third position held by some people.
His words: {وَلَوْ كَانَ}: a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyya); the precise treatment of this was given earlier, and that it is like his words, peace be upon him: «أَعطُوا السائل ولو جاء على فرس» ("Give to the beggar even if he comes on a horse"). «لبعضٍ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ظَهير».

semin-durr:89-89.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا}: its object is omitted. It is also said: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in {مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ}, and that is the object; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and it is the position of the Kufans and al-Akhfash.
Al-Ḥasan read «صَرَفْنا» with the rāʾ undoubled; its like was mentioned earlier.
His words: {إِلاَّ كُفُوراً}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because it is equivalent to: "they did nothing but disbelief".

semin-durr:90-90.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {حتى تَفْجُرَ}: the Kufans read «تَفْجُرَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm undoubled, the imperfect of «فَجَر». The rest read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the fāʾ and kasra on the jīm doubled, the imperfect of فَجَّر for multiplicity. They did not differ about the second one, that it is with doubling, since its maṣdar (verbal noun) is stated explicitly. Al-Aʿmash read «تُفْجِرَ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the fāʾ and kasra on the jīm undoubled, the imperfect of أَفْجر meaning فَجَرَ; so neither the doubling nor the hamza is for making transitive.
«يَنْبوعاً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); its pattern is yafʿūl, because it is from al-nabʿ (gushing); al-yanbūʿ is a spring that wells up from the earth.

semin-durr:91-91.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {خِلالَهَا}: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); its precise treatment was given at the beginning of the sūra.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ تُسْقِطَ}: the majority read with the verb predicated of the one addressed, and «السماءَ» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Mujāhid read with it predicated of «السماء», so it [السماء] is nominative by it.
His words: «كِسْفاً»: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read it here with fatḥa on the sīn, and Ḥafṣ did so in al-Shuʿarāʾ and in Sabaʾ. The rest read with sukūn on it in all three places. Ibn Dhakwān read with sukūn on it in al-Rūm without disagreement, and Hishām has both ways from him [Ibn ʿĀmir]; the rest [read it] with fatḥa.
Whoever reads the sīn with fatḥa makes it the plural of kisfa, like qiṭʿa and qiṭaʿ, kisra and kisar; and whoever reads it with sukūn also makes it the plural of kisfa, in the manner of sidra and sidr, qamḥa and qamḥ.
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two further views in it. First: that it is a plural on the pattern faʿal with fatḥa on the middle radical, and was given sukūn only for lightening. This is not permissible, because the fatḥa is light and can be borne even by a weak letter, where other vowels are [only] implied in it — so how much more by a sound letter? He said: "The second: that it is faʿl in the sense of mafʿūl", like al-ṭaḥn in the sense of maṭḥūn (ground); so for the sukūn [reading] there are three views.
The root meaning of al-kasf is cutting. One says: كَسَفْتُ الثوبَ, "I cut the garment". In the ḥadīth, in the story of Sulaymān with the swift steeds standing on three legs: that he «كَسَفَ عراقيبَها», i.e. cut [their hamstrings]. Al-Zajjāj said: "كَسَفَ الشيء means he covered it." It is said: this is not known from anyone besides him.
Its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). If we make it a plural, it is on [the basis of] omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessing pieces"; if we make it faʿl in the sense of mafʿūl, it needs no implied element; then it may be asked: why was it not made feminine? It is answered: because the femininity of «السماء» is not real, or because it carries the meaning of "roof" (saqf).
His words: «كما زَعَمْتَ»: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a causing-to-fall like what you claimed"; this is how Abū al-Baqāʾ gave its implied form.
His words: «قَبِيْلاً»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الله والملائكة», or of one of them, the ḥāl of the other being omitted, i.e. "with Allah as a guarantor and the angels as a guarantor", as in his words:
310 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . كنتُ منه ووالدي ... بريئاً. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… I was, of it, and my father, innocent …)
[And as in his words:]
310 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنِّي وقَيَّارٌ بها لغريبُ
(… then I — and Qayyār — am indeed a stranger there.)
Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. This is when we make «قبيلاً» mean kafīl, i.e. guarantor, or mean "face to face" as al-Fārisī said. If we make it mean "a company", it is a ḥāl of «الملائكة».
Al-Aʿraj read «قِبَلاً», from muqābala (facing).

semin-durr:93-93.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَوْ ترقى}: an imperfect verb, accusative by implication, because it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تَفَجُّرَ» [Translator's note: so written in the text; the Quranic word is «تَفْجُرَ»], i.e. "or until you ascend into the sky", i.e. into its stairways. Al-ruqiyy is ascending. One says رَقِي with kasra, يَرْقى with fatḥa, ruqiyyan on the pattern fuʿūl — the original being ruquwy, then it was assimilated after the wāw was changed into a yāʾ — and raqyan on the measure of ḍarb. The rajaz poet said:
310 - 8- أنتَ الذي كلَّفْتني رَقْيَ الدَّرجْ ... على الكَلالِ والمَشِيْبِ والعَرَجْ
(You are the one who burdened me with climbing [رقي] the stairs, despite fatigue, grey hair and lameness.)
His words: «نَقْرَؤُه»: two views are possible. First: that it is an adjective of «كتاباً». Second: that it is [a ḥāl (circumstantial)] of the «ن» in «علينا»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this; and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because they would read it only after it is sent down, not at the moment of its being sent down.
His words: {قُلْ سُبْحَانَ}: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read «قال», a past verb, reporting this of the Messenger, peace be upon him; the rest read «قُلْ» as an imperative/, a command from Him the Exalted to His Prophet ﷺ to say that. It is written in the codices of the Meccans and the Syrians «قال» with an alif, and in the codices of the others «قُلْ» without it; so each agreed with his codex.
His words: {إَلاَّ بَشَراً رَّسُولاً}: «بشراً» may be the khabar (predicate) of «كنتُ» and «رسولاً» its adjective; or «رسولاً» may be the khabar and «بَشَراً» a ḥāl fronted before it.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَن يؤمنوا}: «أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا» is the second object of «مَنَع», i.e./ "nothing prevented them [from] their believing", or "from their believing"; «أنْ قالوا» is the fāʿil (agent), and «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «مَنَعَ». The implied form is: "And nothing prevented people from belief, at the time the guidance came to them, except their saying «أَبَعَثَ الله»."
This negated clause may be from the speech of Allah, so it is resumptive; or from the speech of the Messenger, so it is in the position of the accusative, being included under the [verb of] saying, on both readings.
His words: {بَشَراً رَّسُولاً}: [this has] the two views mentioned earlier for its like; and likewise His words {لَنَزَّلْنَا [عَلَيْهِم] مِّنَ السمآء مَلَكاً رَّسُولاً}.

semin-durr:95-95.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَوْ كَانَ فِي الأرض}: this «كان» may be the complete (tāmma) one, i.e. "if there existed and were found"; «يمشون» is an adjective of «ملائكةٌ», {فِي الأرض} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, and «مطمئنين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَمْشُون». It may also be the defective (nāqiṣa) one, and there are several views on its khabar (predicate). The most evident: that it is the preposition-phrase, with «يَمْشُون» and «مطمئنين» as above. It is said: the khabar is «يَمْشُون», and {فِي الأرض} is attached to it. It is said: the khabar is «مطمئنين», and «يَمْشُون» is an adjective. These two views are weak, because the meaning follows the first.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَمَن يَهْدِ الله}: this clause may be included under what is said, so that its position is accusative; or it may be from the speech of Allah, so it has no grammatical position, being resumptive; and there would be a shift (iltifāt) in the discourse, since there is a departure from the third person to the first person in His words «ونَحْشُرهم».
It was construed according to the wording of «مَنْ» in His words «فهو المهتدِ», so it was made singular; and it was construed according to the meaning of the second «مَنْ» in His words {وَمَن يُضْلِلْ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُمْ}, so it was made plural. The point of fittingness in this — and Allah knows best — is that since guidance is a single thing without branching paths, singularity suited it; and since misguidance has many ways, as in {وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ السبل فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَن سَبِيلِهِ} [al-Anʿām: 153], plurality suited plurality. This second construal is among the cases construed according to the meaning even though it is not preceded by a construal according to the wording. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is rare in the Qurʾān", meaning in comparison with the other. Its like is His words {وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ} [Yūnus: 42]. It is possible that what makes this acceptable is that it was preceded by a construal according to the wording, even if in another clause than its own.
Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read keeping the yāʾ of «المُهْتدي» in continuous recitation and dropping it at a pause, and likewise in the one below [i.e. in the following sūra]; the rest dropped it in both cases.
His words: {على وُجُوهِهِمْ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the gathering [نحشرهم], or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object, i.e. "being, and being dragged, upon their faces".
His words: «عُمْياً»: it may be a second ḥāl, or a badal (substitute) of the first — and there is reservation about this, because the kinds of badal appear: [neither] whole for whole, nor part for whole, nor inclusion [Translator's note: the text reads «لأنه تَظْهَرُ أنواعُ البدلِ», "because the kinds of badal appear"; the sense of the following «ولا … ولا» requires "because none of the kinds of badal appears", i.e. «لا تَظْهَرُ»]; or a ḥāl of the nominative pronoun in the preposition-phrase, since it occurs as a ḥāl; or a ḥāl of the genitive pronoun in «وجوهِهم».
His words: {مَّأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}: this clause may be resumptive or circumstantial: either of the accusative pronoun or of the genitive one.
His words: {كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl of «جهنم», the governing element in it being the meaning of "abode" (al-maʾwā).
خَبَتِ النار تَخْبُو: when its flame subsides; when its embers weaken one says خَمَدَتْ; and when it is extinguished entirely one says هَمَدَت. [The poet] said:
301 - 9- وَسْطُه كاليَراعِ أو سُرُجِ المِجْ ... دَلِ حِيْناً يَخْبُو وحِيناً ينيرُ
(Its middle is like fireflies, or the lamps of al-Mijdal: at times it dims [يخبو], at times it shines.)
Another said:
310 - 0- لِمَنْ نارٌ قبيل الصُّبْ ... حِ عند البيتِ ما تَخْبُو
إذا ما أُخْمِدَتْ اُلْقِيْ ... عليها المَنْدَلُ الرَّطْبُ
(Whose is a fire, shortly before dawn, by the House, that does not die down [تخبو]? Whenever it dies down, fresh aloes-wood is thrown upon it.)
Abū ʿAmr, the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Warsh assimilated the tāʾ into the zāy of «زِدْناهم», and the rest pronounced it distinctly.
[Translator's note: the verse numbers «301 - 9» and «310 - 0» are given as they appear in the source; they do not follow the running sequence.]

semin-durr:98-98.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم بِأَنَّهُمْ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), with «بأنَّهم» attached (mutaʿalliq) to "the recompense", i.e. "that aforementioned punishment is their recompense because they …". «جزاؤهم» may be a second mubtadaʾ, the preposition-phrase its khabar, and the clause the khabar of «ذلك». And «جزاؤهم» may be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with «بأنَّهم» the khabar.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His words {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ}, because it is equivalent to "they have indeed seen"; so it is not included in the domain of the [rhetorical] disapproval, but is conjoined to its clause as a whole.
His words: {لاَّ رَيْبَ فِيهِ}: an adjective of «أجَلاً», i.e. "a term not doubted". If the Day of Resurrection is meant by it, the singular is clear; if death is meant by it, it is a generic noun/, since every human being has a term particular to him.
His words: {إَلاَّ كُفُوراً}: discussed just above.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His words: {وَقَضَيْنَآ}: «قَضَى» is transitive by itself: {فَلَمَّا قضى زَيْدٌ مِّنْهَا وَطَراً} [al-Aḥzāb: 37], {فَلَمَّا قضى مُوسَى الأجل} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 29]. It was made transitive here with «إلى» only because it includes the meaning of "We conveyed" and "We revealed", i.e. We conveyed to them the irrevocable decree. What the decree concerns is omitted, i.e. their corruption. And His words «لَتُفْسِدُنَّ» are the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being: "By Allah, you will surely work corruption"; and this oath confirms what the decree concerns. «لَتُفْسِدُنَّ» may also be an answer to His words «وقَضَيْنا», because it was made to include the meaning of an oath; of this is their saying: «قضاء الله لأفعلنَّ» (Allah's decree: I will surely do it), for they treat the decree and the vow like the oath, and both are answered with what the oath is answered with.
The majority read «الكتاب» in the singular, the genus being meant. Ibn Jubayr and Abū al-ʿĀliya read «في الكُتُب» in the plural; they brought it as an explicit plural.
The majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, as the imperfect of «أفسدَ», its object being omitted, its implied form being: "you will surely corrupt the religions". It is also possible that no object is implied, i.e. "you will surely bring about corruption". Ibn ʿAbbās, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī and Jābir ibn Zayd read «لَتُفْسَدُن» in the passive, i.e. others will surely corrupt you, either by leading astray or by conquest. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn, i.e. you will become corrupt of yourselves.
His words: «مَرَّتَيْنِ» is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), governed by «لتُفْسِدُنَّ», because the implied form is: "two times of corruption".
His words: «عُلُوَّاً»: the majority read it with ḍamma on the ʿayn, as the maṣdar of علا يَعْلُو. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «عِلِيَّاً» with kasra on both and with yāʾ; the original is wāw, and it was made weak only according to the less common usage; that is because in the maṣdar on the pattern fuʿūl the more common is soundness, as in عَتا عُتُوَّاً, while weakening is rare, as in {أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرحمن عِتِيّاً} [Maryam: 69] on one of the two views, as will come; but if it is a plural, the more common is weakening, as in «جِثِيَّاً»; and بَهْوٌ وبُهُوُّ and نَجْوٌ ونَجَوٌّ are anomalous, though al-Farrāʾ made them a basis of analogy.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَعْد}: i.e. what is promised; so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a passive participle. Al-Zamakhsharī left it in its state, but with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the promise of the punishment of the first of them". It is also said: الوَعْد is in the sense of الوعيد (threat). And it is said: in the sense of المَوْعِد (appointment), by which the time is meant. So these are four views. And the pronoun refers back to the two times.
His words: «عِباداً»: the majority read «عِباد» on the pattern fiʿāl, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Ḥasan read «عبيداً» on faʿīl; the discussion of that has preceded.
His words: «فجاسُوا» is conjoined to «بَعَثْنا», i.e. this followed upon Our sending them. And الجَوْس and الجُوْس, with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the jīm, are the maṣdar of جاسَ يَجُوسُ, i.e. he searched and probed; Abū ʿUbayd said this. Al-Farrāʾ said: "they killed". Ḥassān said:
302 - 6- ومِنَّا الذي لاقى بسيفِ محمدٍ ... فجاسَ به الأعداءُ عَرْضَ العساكرِ
(And of us is he who met [the foe] with the sword of Muhammad, and with it ransacked the enemies across the breadth of the armies.)
Abū Zayd said: "الجُوس, الجَوْس, الحَوْس and الهَوْس are seeking to roam about at night." And Quṭrub came close [Translator's note: the source has «وقارب قطرب», perhaps a misprint for «وقال قطرب», "Quṭrub said"]: "جاسُوا: they alighted", and recited:
302 - 7- فَجُسْنا ديارَهُمُ عَنْوَةً ... وأُبْنا بساداتِهم مُوْثَقِيْنا
(We trampled their homes by force, and returned with their chiefs bound in fetters.)
It is also said: "جاسُوا in the sense of داسوا (they trampled)", and he recited:
302 - 8- إليك جُسْنا الفِيلَ بالمَطِيِّ ...
(To you we crossed the wilderness on our mounts …)
It is also said: الجَوْس is going back and forth. And it is said: seeking a thing exhaustively. One also says «حاسُوا» with the undotted ḥāʾ, and Ṭalḥa and Abū al-Sammāl read it so; and it was read «فَجَوَّسُوا» with jīm, on the pattern of نُكِّسُوا.
His words: «خلالَ»: the majority read «خِلال», and it admits two views. The first: it is the plural of خَلَل (gap), like جِبال from جَبَل and جِمال from جَمَل. The second: it is a singular noun in the sense of "the midst", and the reading of al-Ḥasan, «خَلَلَ الدِّيار», indicates this. And His words: «وكان وَعْداً», i.e. and the ransacking was, or the promise of the first of them was, or the promise of their punishment was.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
The words of the Exalted: {الكرة}: the object of «رَدَدْنا». It is originally the maṣdar (verbal noun) of كَرَّ يَكُرُّ, i.e. he returned; then it came to express the turn of power and conquest.
His words: «عليهم» may be attached to «رَدَدْنا», or to الكَرَّة itself, because one says كَرَّ عليه (he turned upon him), so it is made transitive with «على»; and it may be attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الكَرَّة».
His words: «نَفِيراً» is in the accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and there are several views on it. The first: it is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. "more numerous in those who go forth", i.e. those who march out with you. The second: it is the plural of نَفْر, like عَبْد and عَبيد; al-Zajjāj said this; and they are the group heading towards the enemies. The third: it is a maṣdar, i.e. more in going out to raid. The poet said:
302 - 9- فَأَكْرِمْ بقَحْطانَ مِنْ والدٍ ... وحِمْيَرَ أكرِمْ بقومٍ نَفيرا
(How noble is Qaḥṭān as an ancestor! And Ḥimyar — how noble a people in marching forth!)
The thing over which preference is given is omitted. Some implied it as: "more numerous in marching forth than your enemies", and al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "more numerous in marching forth than you were".

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَلَهَا}: there are several views on the lām. The first: it is in the sense of «على», i.e. "then upon it", as in his words:
303 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَخَرَّ صريعاً لليدينِ وللفمِ
(… and he fell prostrate on his hands and his mouth.)
i.e. "on the hands". The second: it is in the sense of «إلى». Al-Ṭabarī said: "i.e. to it the evil returns." The third: it has its usual sense, and it was brought instead of «على» only for correspondence with His words «لأنفسِكم», so it was brought for parallelism (izdiwāj). This lām may be attached to an implied verb, as preceded in al-Ṭabarī's words; or [it may be attached] to something omitted, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "then the evil is for it, not for another".
His words: {فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ الآخرة}, i.e. the last time; «المرَّة» (the time) was omitted because it is indicated. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "We sent them".
And His words: {لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ} is attached to this implied apodosis. Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read «لِيَسُوْءَ» with yāʾ with fatḥa and a hamza with fatḥa at the end of the verb. Its fāʿil (agent) is either Allah the Exalted, or the promise, or the sending, or the force (al-nafīr). Al-Kisāʾī read «لِنَسُوءَ» with the nūn of majesty, i.e. "that We may disgrace", and this agrees with what precedes it — His words «بَعَثْنا عباداً لنا», «رَدَدْنا» and «أَمْدَدْنا» — and with what follows — His words «عُدْنا» and «جَعَلْنا».
The rest read «لِيَسُوْءُوا», ascribed to the plural pronoun referring back to the servants, or to the force (al-nafīr), because it is a collective noun; and this agrees with what follows it, in His words {وَلِيَدْخُلُواْ المسجد كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوْاْ}. Referring the pronoun to the nafīr is open to question, because the nafīr mentioned belongs to those addressed, so how can that nafīr be described as disgracing their faces? Unless the one who says this means that it refers back to its wording, not its meaning, in the manner of «عندي درهمٌ ونصفُه» (I have a dirham and half of it).
Ubayy read «لِنَسُوْءَنْ» with the lām of command, the light nūn of emphasis and the nūn of majesty; this is an apodosis of «إذا», but with the omission of the fāʾ, i.e. «فَلِنَسُوْءَنْ»; the lām of command entered the verb of the first person, as in the words of the Exalted: {وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطَايَاكُمْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 12].
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read «لَيَسُوْءَنَّ» and «وَلَنَسوْءَنَّ», with the yāʾ or the nūn of majesty, the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the lām of the oath. In the codex of Ubayy: «لِيَسُوْءُ» with ḍamma on the hamza without wāw; this reading appears to be according to the dialect of those who make do with the ḍamma instead of the wāw, as in his words:
303 - 1- فلوْ أنَّ الأطبَّا كانُ حولي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Were the physicians around me …)
he means «كانوا». And the words of another:
303 - 2- إذا ما الناسُ جاعُ وأَجْدَبُوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When people went hungry and suffered drought …)
he means «جاعُوا». So likewise this reading, i.e. لِيَسُوْءُوا, as in the well-known reading, and the wāw was dropped.
And it was read «لِيَسْيء» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the sīn and a yāʾ after it, i.e. that Allah may make your faces ugly, or the promise, or the sending. And in the codex of Anas: «وَجْهَكم» in the singular, as in his words:
303 - 3- كُلوا في بعضِ بطنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Eat in part of your belly, and you will be abstemious …)
[And as in his words:]
303 - 4-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... في حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقد شَجِيْنا
(… in your throat is a bone, while we have choked.)
[And as in his words:]
303 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . وأمَّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيْبُ
(… as for its skin, it is tough.)
His words: «ولِيَدْخُلُوا»: whoever made the first the lām of kay (purpose) makes this one also the lām of kay, conjoined to it, a conjunction of one reason to another; and whoever made it a lām of command, like Ubayy, or a lām of oath, like ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, then the lām in «لِيَدْخُلوا» admits two views: command and causation. And {كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ} is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of its pronoun, as Sībawayh says, i.e. "an entering like their entering it". And {أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ} is an adverb of time; the discussion of it has preceded in Barāʾa.
[His words:] {مَا عَلَوْاْ}: «ما» may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "that they may destroy what they overcame"; it is also said: "that they may demolish it", as in his words:
303 - 6- وما الناسُ إلا عاملان فعامِلٌ ... يُُتَبِّرُ ما يَبْني وآخرُ رافِعُ
(People are but two kinds of workers: one who destroys what he builds, and another who raises up.)
And it may be adverbial (ẓarfiyya), i.e. for the duration of their supremacy; this requires the omission of an object, unless the intention is merely to mention the act, as in: he gives and withholds.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
The words of the Exalted: {حَصِيراً}: it may be in the sense of fāʿil (active participle), i.e. confining them, encompassing them; on this view it ought to have been made feminine with the tāʾ, like خبيرة. It was answered that it is by way of attribution (al-nasab), i.e. possessing confinement, as in His words: {السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ} [al-Muzzammil: 18], i.e. possessing splitting. It is also said: الحَصِير is the prison. Labīd said:
303 - 7- ومَقامَةٍ غُلْبِ الرجالِ كأنَّهمْ ... جِنٌّ لدى بابِ الحصيرِ قيامُ
(And an assembly of thick-necked men, as though they were jinn standing at the door of the king's enclosure.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "He did not make it feminine because faʿīl is in the sense of fāʿil." This is an oversight on his part, because it would lead to the adjective on the pattern faʿīl, when in the sense of fāʿil, being allowed to drop the tāʾ; and it is not so, because of what has preceded, that faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil must be made feminine, while in the sense of mafʿūl it must be masculine, and what comes anomalously of the two kinds is interpreted. It is also said: it was not made feminine only because the femininity of «جهنَّم» is figurative. It is also said: because it is in the sense of السِّجْن and المَحْبَس (prison). And it is said: because it is in the sense of فِرَاش (a bed).

semin-durr:100-100.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَّوْ أَنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ}: there are three views on it. First — held by al-Zamakhsharī, al-Ḥawfī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Makkī — that the case belongs to the topic of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the governing word), so «أنتم» is nominative by an implied verb which this overt one explains, because «لو» is followed only by a verb, overt or implied. So it is like «إنْ» in the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ المشركين} [al-Tawba: 6], and in his words:
311 - 1- وإن هو لم يَحْمِلْ على النفس ضَيْمَها ... فليس إلى حُسْنِ الثَّناء سبيلُ
(And if he does not make the soul bear its hardship, there is no way to fine praise.)
The original is "لو تملكون"; the verb was omitted because what follows indicates it, so the pronoun — the wāw — became detached, since it could not remain attached after its governing verb was omitted. Similar is «وإن هو لم يَحْمِلْ», the original being "وإن لم يَحْمل"; when the verb was omitted, that latent pronoun became detached and appeared. Similar to our case is the poet's saying «لو ذاتُ سِوارٍ لَطَمَتْني» ("Had one wearing a bracelet slapped me"), and the verse of al-Mutalammis:
311 - 2- ولو غيرُ أَخْوالي أرادُوا نَقِيْصَتي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Had others than my maternal uncles sought to disparage me …)
So «ذاتُ سوار» is nominative by a verb explained by the overt one after it.
Second: that it is nominative by «كان», whose omission after «لو» is frequent; the implied form is "لو كنتم تملكون"; «كان» was omitted, so the pronoun became detached, and «تملكون» is in the position of the accusative by «كان». This is the view of Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh. Close to it is his words:
311 - 3- أبا خُراشَةَ أمَّا أنتَ ذا نَفَرٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O Abū Khurāsha, since you are a man with a band of kinsmen …)
For the original is "لأَنْ كنتَ"; «كان» was omitted and the pronoun became detached — except that here «ما» was substituted for «كان», whereas with «لو» no substitute was given for it.
Third: that «أنتم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun of «كان» implied with it, the original being "لو كنتم أنتم تملِكُون"; «كان» and its noun were omitted and the emphasizer remained. This is the view of Ibn Faḍḍāl al-Mujāshiʿī. There is reservation about it, in that we would be omitting [something] in emphasis, even though Sībawayh permits it.
What drove these two to this was that the position of the Basrans regarding «لو» is that it is followed only by an overt verb, and according to them it may not be followed by an implied, explained one except [Translator's note: the text has «إلى», read as «إلا»] in poetic necessity or rarely, as in his words «لو ذاتَ سِوَارٍ لطمَتْني». If it is said: these two views also involve the implication of a verb — it is said: that is not the implication meant; for the implication they rejected is [implication] on condition of explanation (ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr) with verbs other than «كان»; as for «كان», its omission after «لو» is frequent in many places. An explicit noun has occurred after «لو» with no verb mentioned after it; al-Fārisī cited:
311 - 4- لو بغيرِ الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... كنت كالغصَّانِ بالماءِ اعتصاري
(Were my throat choking on something other than water, I would be like one choking on water [who seeks] relief.)
— except that he explained it as being nominative by an implied verb which the adjective in his words «شَرِقٌ» explains. The precise treatment of «لو» was given earlier, so let us confine ourselves to this.
His words: {لأمْسَكْتُمْ}: it may be intransitive because it includes the meaning of "you would have been miserly", or transitive with its object omitted — "you would have withheld wealth"; and it may be like His words {يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ} [al-Baqara: 258].
His words: {خَشْيَةَ الإنفاق}: there are two views on it. The more evident: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
Second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, i.e. "fearing spending". There is reservation about it, since a definite maṣdar does not occur in the place of a ḥāl except by [attested] hearing, as in «جَهْدَك» and «طاقتَك» and [as in his words]:
311 - 5- وأرسلها العِراك. . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And he sent them [to water] crowding together [العراك] …)
and analogy is not drawn on it. Al-infāq is the maṣdar of أنفق, i.e. to spend out wealth. Abū ʿUbayda said: "It means becoming poor and impoverished."

semin-durr:101-101.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تِسْعَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ}: «بيِّنات» may be accusative as an adjective of the number, or genitive as an adjective of the counted.
His words: {إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ}: there are several views on it. First: that it is governed by «آتَيْنا», and His words {فَسْئَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ} are parenthetical. Second: that it is accusative by an implied "remember" (اذكُرْ). Third: that it is accusative by an implied "they inform you" (يُخْبرونك). Fourth: that it is accusative by an implied [verb of] saying, since the implied form is: "So We said to him: ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these views, arranged on a preliminary that he mentioned before that, so let us mention it. He said: "{فَسْئَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ}, i.e. so We said to him: ask the Children of [Israel], i.e. ask them [i.e. ask for them] from Pharaoh, and say/ to him: send the Children of Israel with me; or ask them about their faith and the state of their religion; or ask them to support you. The reading of the Messenger of Allah «فسال», in the form of the past without hamza — and it is the dialect of Quraysh — indicates this.
"It is also said: so ask, O Messenger of Allah, the believer among the Children of Israel, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, about the signs, so that they increase in certainty and tranquillity, as in His words {وَلَكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي} [al-Baqara: 260]." Then he said: "If you say: to what is «إذ جاءهم» attached? I say: on the first view, to the omitted [verb of] saying, i.e. so We said to him: ask them, when he came to them; or to «سال» in the second reading. On the last view, to «آتَيْنا», or to an implied 'remember', or to 'they inform you'. The meaning of 'when he came to them' is: when he came to their forefathers." End of quotation.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Its attachment to «اذكر» or to يُخبرونك is not feasible, because it is an adverb of the past." I say: when he makes it governed by «اذكُرْ» or by يُخْبرونك, he does not make it an adverb but a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as has been established more than once.
Fifth: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, its governing element being «فَسَلْ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There are two views on it. First: it is a mafʿūl bihi of 'ask' according to the meaning, because the meaning is: mention to the Children of Israel [when he came to them]. It is also said: the implied form is 'remember when he came to them', and this is other than the «اذكر» by which you rendered 'ask'." He means that the implied 'remember' is other than the «اذكر» by which you explained «اسأَلْ». This supports what I mentioned to you: that when they assume «اذكر», they make «إذ» a mafʿūl bihi, not an adverb.
However, Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned, in the case of its being an adverb, something that requires a future verb to govern it. He said: "The second: that it is an adverb. There are several views on what governs it. First: «آتَيْنا». Second: an implied «قلنا». Third: «قُلْ», its implied form being: say to your adversary: ask — what is meant by him being Pharaoh — i.e. say, O Moses. The proper way would have been to say 'when you came to them' (إذ جئتهم) with fatḥa [on the tāʾ]; so it returned from the second person to the third."
I say: the apparent sense of the third view is that the governing element is «قُلْ», while it [إذ] is an adverb of the past. Besides, this meaning he inclined to is nothing, since it comes down to: "O Moses, say to Pharaoh: ask the Children of Israel", so Pharaoh would be the one asking the Children of Israel, and that is certainly not what is meant. On the implied form I gave earlier from al-Zamakhsharī — namely that the meaning is "O Moses, ask [for] the Children of Israel, i.e. demand them from Pharaoh" — the first object of the asking is omitted and the second is «بني إسرائيل», the implied form being "ask Pharaoh for the Children of Israel". On this basis the case may be one of tanāzuʿ (two governing words contending for one element), with the second given the governing: since the implied form is "ask Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said", the second was given the governing so the fāʿil (agent) was made nominative by it, and the object of the first was omitted; and this is the preferred of the two positions.
The apparent sense is other than all of this: that the one commanded to ask is our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him, and the Children of Israel were his contemporaries.
The pronoun in {إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ} is either for the forefathers, or for them with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "he came to their forefathers".
His words: «مَسْحُوراً»: there are two views on it. The more evident: that it has its original meaning, i.e. "you have been bewitched, and therefore your speech is disordered"; he said that when he brought him what his wicked soul did not desire. Second: that it has the meaning of fāʿil (active), like maymūn and mashʾūm, i.e. "you are a sorcerer; that is why you bring wonders", alluding to his staff turning into a snake and other things.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ}: al-Kisāʾī read with ḍamma on the tāʾ, predicating the verb of the pronoun of Moses, peace be upon him, i.e. "I am certain that what I have brought is sent down from Allah". The rest read with fatḥa, predicating it of the pronoun of Pharaoh, i.e. "you are certain that what I have brought is sent down from Allah, and your disbelief is only obstinacy". It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he rejected the fatḥa and said: "The enemy of Allah never knew; it was Moses who knew." The negated clause is in the position of the accusative, because it suspends (tuʿalliq) the [verb of] knowing before it.
His words: «بَصائر»: a ḥāl (circumstantial), and there are two opinions about what governs it. First: that it is this uttered «أَنْزَلَ», and the owner of the ḥāl is «هؤلاء»; al-Ḥawfī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ held this, and these permit what precedes «إلا» to govern what follows it even if it is not the excepted, nor that from which exception is made, nor a follower of it. Second — and it is the position of the majority — that what follows «إلا» cannot be governed by what precedes it, so a governing element is implied for it, its implied form being "He sent them down as insights". The like of this was given earlier in Hūd, at His words {إِلاَّ الذين هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ الرأي} [Hūd: 27].
His words: «مَثْبورا»: «مَثْبوراً» is the second object, and the vocative is interposed between the two objects. Al-mathbūr is the one destroyed; one says: ثَبَره اللهُ, i.e. "Allah destroyed him". Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said:
311 - 6- إذ أُجاريْ الشيطانَ في سَنَنِ الغَيْ ... يِ ومَنْ مالَ مَيْلَه مَثْبورُ
(When I kept pace with Satan in the ways of error — and whoever inclines as he inclines is destroyed [مثبور].)
Al-thubūr is destruction; Allah the Exalted said: {لاَّ تَدْعُواْ اليوم ثُبُوراً وَاحِداً} [al-Furqān: 14].

semin-durr:104-104.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {لَفِيفاً}: there are two views on it. First: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that its origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of لفَّ يَلُفُّ لفيفاً, like al-nadhīr and al-nakīr, i.e. "We brought you joined to one another", from لفَّ الشيءَ يَلُفُّه لَفَّاً (to wrap together); al-alaff is one whose thighs are close together, and it is said: one with a big belly. Second: that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording, the meaning being "We brought you all together", so it is equivalent to a tawkīd (emphasis).

semin-durr:105-105.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وبالحق أَنْزَلْنَاهُ}: there are three views on the preposition-phrase. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَنْزَلْناه, the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "We sent it down because of the truth". Second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «أنزلناه», i.e. "with the truth accompanying it". Third: that it is a ḥāl of its fāʿil (agent), i.e. "invested with the truth". On these two views it is attached to an omitted element.
The pronoun in «أَنْزَلْناه»: the apparent view is that it refers to the Qurʾān: either the one uttered in His words before that {على أَن يَأْتُواْ بِمِثْلِ هذا القرآن} [al-Isrāʾ: 88] — this then following the norm of their styles of speech, namely that the speaker digresses into mentioning something his speech was not initially about and then returns to his first speech — or the Qurʾān not previously uttered, because the context indicates it, as in the words of Allah the Exalted {إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ القدر} [al-Qadr: 1]. It is said: it refers to Moses, as in His words {وَأَنزْلْنَا الحديد} [al-Ḥadīd: 25]. It is said: to the promise. It is said: to the nine signs, the pronoun being made masculine and singular by construal according to the meaning of "the proof" and "the demonstration".
His words: {وبالحق نَزَلَ}: it has the first two views, but not the third, because there is no other pronoun besides the pronoun of the Qurʾān. There are two views on this clause. First: that it is for emphasis; that is because one says "I sent it down and it came down" and "I sent it down and it did not come down", so His words {وبالحق نَزَلَ} were brought to remove this misconception. It is also said: it is not for emphasis, and the difference is achieved by the difference between the two "truths": the first truth is tawḥīd (divine oneness), and the second is the promise and the threat, the command and the prohibition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "We did not send down the Qurʾān except with the wisdom that required its sending down, and it did not come down except invested with truth and wisdom, since it contains guidance to every good; or: We did not send it down from heaven except with the truth, guarded by watchers from among the angels, and it did not come down upon the Messenger except guarded by them from the confusion [mixed in] by the devils." And «مبشِّراً ونذيراً» are two ḥāls of the object of «أَرْسَلْنَاك».

semin-durr:9-9.t: The words of the Exalted: {لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ}: i.e. to the state, or to the religion, or to the way [that is most upright]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whichever you imply, you will not find, with stating it, the taste of eloquence that you find with the omission, because of the grandeur in leaving the described noun vague by omitting it, which is lost when it is made explicit."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وأَنَّ الذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is conjoined to the first «أنَّ», i.e. He gives the believers glad tidings of two things: of a great reward and of the punishment of their enemies; and there is no doubt that what befalls your enemy is a joy for you. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that what is meant is: and He informs that those who …"
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Then it would not be included under the glad tidings." I say: al-Zamakhsharī's words admit two things. The first: that his saying "it is possible that what is meant is: and He informs that …" is a case of omission, i.e. He omitted "and He informs" and kept what it governs; on this view «أنَّ الذين» is not within the scope of the glad tidings, without doubt. And it is possible that his intention is that by "glad tidings" mere informing is meant, whether of good or of evil — and whether it is literal in both or in one of them; in that case it would be combining the literal and the figurative, or using a homonym in both its meanings, and in both questions there is a well-known disagreement. On this view His words {وأَنَّ الذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} would not be outside the scope of the glad tidings. However, the apparent position of al-Zamakhsharī is that he permits neither combining the literal and the figurative nor using a homonym in both its meanings.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَدْعُ الإنسان بالشر دُعَآءَهُ بالخير}: there are three views on the two bāʾs. The first: they are both attached to the supplication, in their usual sense, as in «دَعَوْتُ بكذا» (I prayed for such-and-such). The meaning is that man, in his state of vexation, may pray for evil and insist on it, just as he prays [for good] and insists on it.
The second: they are in the sense of «في» (concerning), meaning that when harm afflicts a man he prays, insists in prayer and seeks to hasten relief, like the prayer he would love to make in a state of well-being; on this view what is prayed for is neither the evil nor the good. This is far-fetched. The third: they are causal; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and the meaning does not support it. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its fāʿil (agent).

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of the Exalted: {آيَتَيْنِ}: it may be the first object, with {الليل والنهار} as two adverbs in the position of the second, placed before the first; the implied form is: "and We made two signs in the night and the day". By the two signs is meant either the sun and the moon, or the wrapping of this over that and that over this. Or «آيَتَيْن» may be the second [object], and {الليل والنهار} the first. Then there are two possibilities. The first: it involves the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first, i.e. "the two luminaries of the night and the day", namely the moon and the sun; or from the second, i.e. "possessing two signs". The second: there is no omission, and they are two signs in themselves, indicating something else. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That is why He annexed in one place and qualified in another", meaning that He annexed the sign to them in His words {آيَةَ الليل} and {الليل والنهار}, and in another place qualified them as being two, in His words: «وجَعَلْنا الليلَ والنهارَ آيتين». All this is if we make الجَعْل "transforming", transitive to two objects. But if we make it in the sense of "We created", «آيتين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
Some found it problematic that «جَعَلَ» should be in the sense of صَيَّر (transform), saying: "Because it would require that the night and the day existed in one state, then moved from it to another."
His words: «مُبْصِرَةً»: there are several views on it. The first: it is a case of figurative predication (isnād majāzī), because the seeing in it belongs to its people, as in His words: {وَآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ الناقة مُبْصِرَةً} [al-Isrāʾ: 59], since it was a cause of seeing. It is also said: «مُبْصِرة» means shining. It is also said: it is of the afʿala pattern by which someone other than the one to whom the verb is ascribed is meant, as in their saying: «أَضْعَفَ الرجلُ», i.e. his livestock became weak, and «أَجْبن» when his family are cowards; so the meaning is that its people are seeing.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and Qatāda read «مَبْصَرة» with fatḥa on the mīm and the ṣād; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a noun, and this is frequent in descriptions of places, as in «مَذْأَبَة» (a place full of wolves).
His words: {وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is in the accusative by ishtighāl (the verb being occupied with a pronoun), the accusative being preferred because a verbal clause precedes. Likewise {وَكُلَّ إِنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 13]. The second — and it is far-fetched: it is in the accusative, conjoined to «الحِسابَ», i.e. that you may know everything as well; on this view «فَصَّلْناه» is an adjective.
And it was read «في عُنْقِه», which is a common lightening.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَنُخْرِجُ}: the majority read «نُخْرِجُ» with the nūn of majesty, the imperfect of «أَخْرَجَ». And regarding «كتاباً» there are two views. The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The second: it is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted object, since the implied form is: "and We bring it out to him as a book", and We bring out the omen (al-ṭāʾir).
It is related from Abū Jaʿfar: «ويُخْرَجُ» in the passive, with «كتاباً» in the accusative as a ḥāl, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being the pronoun of the omen. And from him that he read «كتاباً» in the nominative; this was explained as being nominative by the passive verb. The first is an awkward reading.
Al-Ḥasan read «ويَخْرُجُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ, the imperfect of «خَرَجَ», with «كتابٌ» as its fāʿil (agent). Ibn Muḥayṣin and Mujāhid read likewise, except that they put «كتاباً» in the accusative as a ḥāl, the agent being the pronoun of the omen, i.e. and his omen comes out for him in this state. And it was read «ويُخْرِجُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, the imperfect of «أَخْرَجَ», the agent being the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, and «كتاباً» the object.
His words: «يَلْقَاْه» is an adjective of «كتاباً», and «مَنْشُوراً» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ of «يَلْقاه». Al-Zamakhsharī, the Shaykh and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب. This is open to question, inasmuch as it entails placing a non-explicit (clausal) adjective before an explicit one, and what is involved in that has preceded.
Ibn ʿĀmir read «يُلَقَّاه» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the lām and doubling of the qāf, the imperfect of «لَقَّى» with doubling; and the rest with fatḥa, sukūn and without doubling, the imperfect of لَقِي.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
The words of the Exalted: {اقرأ}: with an implied verb of saying, i.e. it will be said to him: read. This saying is either an adjective or a ḥāl (circumstantial), as in the clause before it.
His words: {كفى بِنَفْسِكَ}: there are three views on it. The one well known among the parsers: «كفى» is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is the noun put in the genitive by the bāʾ, which is redundant (zāʾida) in it. What indicates this is that [when] it is dropped, it becomes nominative, as in his words:
303 - 8- ويُخْبرني عن غائبٍ المَرْءِ هَدْيُه ... كَفَى الهَدْيُ عَمَّا غَيَّبَ المَرْءُ مُخْبِرا
(A man's conduct tells me of what is hidden in him; conduct suffices as an informant about what a man conceals.)
And the words of another:
303 - 9-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كَفَى الشيبُ والإِسلامُ للمرءِ ناهيا
(… grey hair and Islam suffice as restrainers for a man.)
On this view the verb ought to have been made feminine because its agent is feminine, even though it is in the genitive, as in His words: {مَآ آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْيَةٍ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 6] and {وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Anʿām: 4]. It may be said that it came according to one of the two permissible options, for the femininity is figurative. The second: the agent is the pronoun of the one addressed, and «كفى» on this view is a noun of an imperative verb (ism fiʿl amr), i.e. "be sufficed"; this is weak, because «كَفَى» accepts the signs of verbs. The third: the agent of «كَفَى» is a pronoun referring back to the sufficing; the discussion of this has preceded in full. And «اليومَ» is in the accusative by «كفى».
His words: «حَسِيْبا»: there are two views on it. The first: it is a tamyīz (specification).
