Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is in the sense of حاسِب (reckoner), like ضَرِيْب القِداح in the sense of the one who casts the arrows, and صَرِيْم in the sense of صارِم; Sībawayh mentioned both. And «على» is attached to it, from your saying: حَسِب عيله كذا [Translator's note: so printed; read «عليه», 'he counted such-and-such against him']. It may also be in the sense of الكافي (the sufficer), put in the place of الشهيد (the witness), so it is made transitive with «على», because the witness spares the claimant what concerns him. If you say: why did He make «حسيباً» masculine? I say: because it is in the position of the witness, the judge and the trustee, and these are matters men undertake; so it is as though it were said: your soul suffices as a reckoning man. And النفس may also be interpreted in the sense of 'person', as one says: 'three souls (anfus)'." I say: of this are the words of the poet:
304 - 0- ثلاثةُ أنفسٍ وثلاثُ ذَوْدٍ ... لقد جارَ الزمانُ على عيالي
(Three souls and three camels — time has indeed wronged my household.)
The second: it is in the accusative as a ḥāl, and it is masculine for the reason given above. It is also said: حَسِيب is in the sense of مُحاسِب (one who calls to account), like خَلِيط and جَلِيس in the sense of مُخالِط and مُجالِس.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَمَرْنَا}: the majority read it short (without the long vowel) and without doubling, and there are two views on it. The first: it is from الأمر (command), the opposite of prohibition. Those who hold this then differed about what this command concerns. From Ibn ʿAbbās, among others: that it means "We commanded them to obey, and they acted immorally". Al-Zamakhsharī rejected this strongly and denounced it emphatically in a long passage, the gist of which is that it is an omission of something for which there is no evidence. He himself implied that the command concerns immorality, i.e. "We commanded them to act immorally". He said: "i.e. We commanded them to act immorally, and they did; the command is figurative, because the reality of commanding them to act immorally is that He should say to them: 'act immorally', and this does not happen; so it remains that it is figurative. The aspect of the figure is that He poured blessings upon them abundantly, and they made them a means to sins and to following desires; so it is as though they were commanded to do that, because the bestowal of the blessing was a cause of it; whereas He only granted them the blessings that they might give thanks."
Then he said: "If you say: why did you not claim that its meaning is: We commanded them to obey, and they acted immorally? I say: because omitting something for which there is no evidence is not permissible; so how about omitting something when the evidence stands for its contrary? That is because the thing commanded is omitted only because «فَفَسَقُوا» indicates it. It is common speech: one says «أَمَرْتُه فَقام» (I commanded him and he stood) and «أَمَرْتُه فَقَرأ» (I commanded him and he recited); nothing is understood from it except that the thing commanded was standing or reciting; and if you set out to imply something else, you would be demanding knowledge of the unseen from the one you address. This is not refuted by their saying «أَمَرْتُه فعصاني» (I commanded him and he disobeyed me) or «فلم يمتثلْ» (and he did not comply), because that is incompatible with the command and contradicts it, and what contradicts the command cannot be the thing commanded; so it is impossible that it should be intended at all, so as to be made indicative of the thing commanded. Thus the thing commanded in this speech is neither intended nor meant, because one who speaks this speech does not intend for his command a thing commanded; it is as though he were saying: there was a command from me, and there was obedience from him — just as one who says: '[So-and-so] commands and forbids, gives and withholds' [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «يبأمرُ» for «يأمرُ»] does not intend an object. If you say: why was not the established knowledge that Allah does not command indecency evidence that what is meant is: We commanded them to do good? I say: because His words «فَفَسَقوا» repel it; it would be as though you expressed one thing while implying its opposite. The parallel of «أمر» is «شاء» (to will), in that the omission of its object is common because what follows indicates it. You say: 'had he willed, he would have done good to you', and 'had he willed, he would have done you harm', meaning: had he willed the doing of good, and had he willed the doing of harm. And if you set out to imply the opposite of what you expressed, and said: the state of the one to whom the willing is ascribed shows that he is of the people of doing good, or of the people of doing harm, so leave the outward spoken words and imply what the state of the one to whom the willing is ascribed indicates — you would not be on the right course."
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] followed him up on this and said: "As for the figurative interpretation he adopted, it is very far-fetched. As for his saying: 'because omitting something for which there is no evidence is not permissible', it is a justification that is not valid in what we are dealing with; rather there is something that indicates its omission.
As for his saying: 'so how can something be omitted when the evidence stands for its contrary' up to 'knowledge of the unseen', we say: omitting a thing is sometimes because something agreeing with it indicates it — and of this is what he gave as an example in his saying 'I commanded him and he stood' — and sometimes because something differing from it, or its opposite, or its contradictory indicates it, as in the words of the Exalted: {وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي اليل والنهار} [al-Anʿām: 13], i.e. what is still and what moves; and His words: {سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81], i.e. and the cold; and the words of the poet:
304 - 1- وما أَدْرِيْ إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضاً ... أريدُ الخيرَ ايُّهما يَلِينْي
أالخيرُ الذي أنا أَبْتَغِيْهِ ... أم الشرُّ الذي هو يَبْتَغيني
(I do not know, when I head for a land seeking good, which of the two will befall me: the good that I seek, or the evil that seeks me?)
i.e. and I avoid evil. And you say: «أَمَرْتُه فلم يُحْسِنْ» (I commanded him and he did not do well); the meaning is not: I commanded him not to do well; rather the meaning is: I commanded him to do well, and he did not do well. The verse is of this kind: the omission of the contradictory is inferred from its contradictory, just as the omission of the like is inferred from its like. Likewise «أَمَرْتُه فأساء إليَّ» (I commanded him and he wronged me): the meaning is not: I commanded him to wrong me, but: I commanded him to do good. As for his saying: 'This is not refuted by their saying: I commanded him and he disobeyed me', we say: rather it is refuted by it. As for his saying: 'because that is incompatible', i.e. because disobedience is incompatible — that is correct speech. As for his saying: 'so the thing commanded is neither indicated nor intended', it is not conceded; rather it is indicated and intended — not by indication of what agrees but by indication of what contradicts, as we have explained. As for his saying: 'he does not intend a thing commanded', it is not conceded. As for his saying: 'because «فَفَسَقُوا» repels it', to the end, we say: yes, he intends one thing and expresses its opposite, because its contradictory indicates it. As for his saying: 'the parallel of «أمر» is «شاء»', it is not its parallel, because the object of «أمر» is frequently stated explicitly. Allah [the Exalted] said: {إِنَّ الله لاَ يَأْمُرُ بالفحشآء} [al-Aʿrāf: 28], {أَمَرَ أَلاَّ تعبدوا إِلاَّ إِيَّاهُ} [Yūsuf: 40], {يَأْمُرُ بالعدل} [al-Naḥl: 67] [Translator's note: so referenced in the source; the phrase occurs in al-Naḥl 76 and 90], {أَمَرَ رَبِّي بالقسط} [al-Aʿrāf: 29], {أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلاَمُهُمْ بهاذآ} [al-Ṭūr: 32]; and the poet said:
304 - 2- أَمَرْتُك الخيرَ فافْعَلْ ما أُمِرْتَ به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I commanded you to do good, so do what you were commanded …)"
I say: the Shaykh rebutted him as one who rests from reflection; were it not for fear of wearying the reader, there would be room for examining the words of both of them.
The second view: «أَمَرْنا» is in the sense of "We multiplied". Al-Zamakhsharī was not pleased with it, judging by the apparent sense of his wording, for he said: "Some explained «أَمَرْنا» as «كَثَّرْنا» (We multiplied), and made it of the pattern 'I did X to it, so it underwent X' (faʿaltuhu fa-faʿala), like ثَبَرْتُه فَثَبَر (I destroyed it and it perished). And in the hadith: 'The best wealth is a well-pollinated row of palms (sikka maʾbūra) and a fertile foal (muhra maʾmūra)', i.e. abundant in offspring." I say: Abū Ḥātim related this usage: one says أَمِر القومُ (the people became many) and أَمَرهم اللهُ (Allah multiplied them); al-Wāḥidī also transmitted it from the lexicographers. Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī] said: "The good view regarding «أَمَرْنا» is that it is in the sense of 'We multiplied'."
Abū ʿUbayda adduced as evidence what came in the hadith, and mentioned it. One says: أَمَرَ اللهُ المُهْرَة, i.e. He multiplied her offspring. He said: "And whoever denies «أمرَ اللهُ القومَ», i.e. multiplied them, is not to be heeded, since that is established in the language."
It would then be one of the verbs that are intransitive and transitive through differing vowels, since one says أَمِر القومُ, they became many, and أَمَرَهم الله, He multiplied them; and it is of the pattern of compliance (al-muṭāwaʿa): أَمَرهم الله فَأْتَمَروا, as in your saying: شَتَرَ اللهُ عَيْنَه فَشَتِرَتْ (Allah split his eyelid and it was split), جَدَعَ أَنْفَه فَجَدِع (He cut off his nose and it was cut off), and ثَلَمَ سِنَّه فَثَلِمَتْ (He chipped his tooth and it was chipped).
Al-Ḥasan, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and ʿIkrima read «أَمِرْنا» with kasra on the mīm, in the sense of «أَمَرْنا» with fatḥa. Abū Ḥātim related from Abū Zayd that one says: «أَمَرَ اللهُ مالَه، وأَمِرَه» (Allah increased his wealth), with fatḥa and kasra on the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ rejected this reading, and his rejection is not to be heeded, since it is established as a usage through the transmission of trustworthy authorities. Abū Jaʿfar and Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī in his Lawāmiḥ transmitted it as a reading from Ibn ʿAbbās — so how can it be rejected?
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Abū Rajāʾ, among others, read «آمَرْنا» with the long vowel; this was also related as a reading from Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ, and Yaʿqūb chose it; the hamza in it is for transitivity.
ʿAlī also, Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī read «أمَّرْنا» with doubling. There are two views on it. The first: the doubling is for transitivity; He made it transitive once with the hamza and another time by doubling the ʿayn, like أَخْرَجْته and خَرَّجته. The second: it is in the sense of "We made them commanders (umarāʾ)", the intransitive of which is «أُمِّر». Al-Fārisī said: "There is no way for «أَمَّرْنا» to be from الإمارة (command, rulership), because their leadership can only belong to one after another, whereas the destruction happens in a single period." Al-Fārisī was rebutted on the grounds that we do not concede that the amīr is the king, such that what you said would follow, because the amīr among the Arabs is one who commands and whose command is followed. And even if that were conceded, what he said does not follow, because when a man of luxury rules and acts immorally, then another after him acts immorally, and so on, the corruption increases, and [destruction] descends upon them in the time of the last of their kings.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ}: there are several views on its accusative. First: that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We gave you a Qurʾān", indicated by His words {وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا موسى} [al-Isrāʾ: 101]. Second: that it is accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the kāf in «أَرْسَلْناك». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In that the sending of this one and the sending down of this one are a single meaning."
Third: that it is accusative, conjoined to {مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً}. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is accusative by «أَرْسَلْناك», i.e. We sent you only as a bearer of good tidings, a warner and a Qurʾān, as you would say: 'and a mercy', because the Qurʾān is a mercy." I say: he means that the Qurʾān itself was made to mean mercy, by way of hyperbole; had he claimed this on [the basis of] omission of a muḍāf it would have been closer, i.e. "and possessor of a Qurʾān". These two views are strained.
Fourth: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the governing word), i.e. "and We divided a Qurʾān, We divided it". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] excused this — i.e. its being such that, had we made it a mubtadaʾ (subject), beginning with it would not be valid for lack of a justifying factor, since ishtighāl is permitted only where that noun may serve as a mubtadaʾ — by [saying] that there is an omitted adjective there, its implied form being "and a Qurʾān — what a Qurʾān!", meaning a mighty one. On this view «فَرَقْناه» has no grammatical position, unlike the preceding views, for [on them] its position is accusative, being an adjective of «قرآناً».
The majority read «فَرَقْناه» undoubled, i.e. "We made clear its lawful and its unlawful", or "We distinguished in it between truth and falsehood". ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah honour his face — Ubayy, ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda and Ḥumayd, among others, read it doubled. There are two views on this. First: that the doubling is for multiplicity, i.e. "We divided its verses among command and prohibition, wisdom and rulings, admonitions and parables, stories and reports past and future". Second: that it indicates dividing up and revelation in instalments (tanjīm).
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read it doubled and said: it did not come down in two days or in three; rather, there were twenty years between its first and its last — meaning that «فَرَقَ» undoubled indicates a close separation."
The Shaykh said: "One of those who chose that — meaning tanjīm — said: it did not come down in a day or two days, nor in a month or two months, nor in a year or two years. Ibn ʿAbbās said: there were twenty years between its first and its last. Thus did al-Zamakhsharī report from Ibn ʿAbbās." I say: the apparent sense of/ this is that the view of tanjīm is not narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — especially since he separated his phrase "Ibn ʿAbbās said" from his phrase "one of those who chose that said". His purpose was that he did not attribute it to Ibn ʿAbbās, so that his refutation of al-Zamakhsharī might hold, namely that faʿʿala with doubling does not indicate dividing up; he had this discussion with him earlier at the beginning of this topic.
His words: «لتقرأَه»: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «فَرَقْناه». «على مُكْثٍ»: there are three views on it. First: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) or the object in «لتقرأه», i.e. "unhurried, deliberate".
Second: that it is a badal (substitute) of «على الناس»; al-Ḥawfī said this, and it is a mistake, because «على مُكْثٍ» is, in terms of meaning, among the attributes of the reader or the thing read, not among the attributes of the people, such that it could be a badal of them. Third: that it is attached to «فَرَقْناه».
The Shaykh said: "The apparent view is that «على مُكْث» is attached to His words «لتقرأه»; and it does not matter that the verb has two prepositions of one kind attached to it, because the meanings of the two prepositions differ: the first is in the position of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the second in the position of the ḥāl, i.e. unhurried, deliberate."
I say: his saying first that it is attached to His words «لتقرأَه» contradicts his saying "in the position of the ḥāl", because whenever it is a ḥāl it is attached to an omitted element. It cannot be said that he meant attachment in meaning, not technical attachment, because he said: "and it does not matter that the verb has two prepositions of [one] kind attached to it", and this is an explanation of iʿrāb, not an explanation of meaning.
Al-mukth is lengthiness of duration, and it has three dialectal forms: ḍamma and fatḥa — al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ reported its being read with both — and kasra, which, as far as I know, has not been read. In its verb there are fatḥa and ḍamma, and both will come, Allah the Exalted willing, in al-Naml.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِلأَذْقَانِ}: there are three views on this lām. First: that it means «على» (upon), i.e. "upon the chins", as they say: "he fell down upon his face". Second: that it is for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the particle of superiority [على] has an evident meaning when you say 'he fell upon his face and upon his chin', so what is the meaning of the lām in «خِرَّ لذَقْنَه ولوجهه»? [The poet] said:
311 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فخرَّ صريعاً لليدين وللفمِ
(… and he fell down prostrate on [lām] his hands and his mouth.)
I say: its meaning is: he made his chin and his face [the place] for falling and specified it for it, because the lām is for specification." Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَخِرُّون», and the lām has its basic meaning, i.e. abasing [themselves] to the chins."
Al-adhqān is the plural of dhaqan, the meeting point of the two jawbones. The poet said:
311 - 8- فَخَرُّوا لأَذْقانِ الوجوه تنوشُهُمْ ... سِباعٌ من الطير العوادِي وتَنْتِفُ
(So they fell upon [lām] the chins of their faces, with birds of prey, the attackers, seizing them and plucking.)
«سُجَّداً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «للأَذقان» to be a ḥāl; he said: "i.e. prostrating to the chins". It seems he means by this the second «للأذقان», because otherwise the meaning would become "prostrating to the chins, prostrate"; and for that reason he said: "The third: that it — meaning the lām — means «على»; on this view it is a ḥāl of «يَبْكُون», and «يَبْكُون» is a ḥāl."
[Translator's note: the text writes the quoted phrase as «خِرَّ لذَقْنَه»; the intended form is «خَرَّ لذَقَنِه».]

semin-durr:109-109.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَيَزِيدُهُمْ}: the fāʿil (agent) of «يزيد» is either the Qurʾān, or the weeping, or the prostration, or what is recited, as indicated by His words «إذ يتْلى». The falling down was repeated because its state differs, with weeping and with prostration. The first ḥāl (circumstantial) came as a noun because it indicates stability, and the second as a verb because it indicates renewal and occurrence.

semin-durr:110-110.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَيّاً مَّا تَدْعُواْ}: «أيَّاً» is accusative by «تَدْعُوا» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted, i.e. "whichever of the two names". «تَدْعوا» is jussive by it, so it is both governing and governed, and likewise the verb. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the nominal clause in His words {فَلَهُ الأسمآء الحسنى}. It is also said: it is omitted, its implied form being "it is permissible", and then He began anew, saying: "To Him belong the most beautiful names." This is nothing.
The tanwīn in «أَيَّاً» is a substitute for the muḍāf ilayhi. There are two opinions about «ما». First: that it is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. Second: that it is conditional, the two [conditional words] being combined for emphasis, as two prepositions are combined for emphasis, made acceptable by the difference in wording, as in his words:
311 - 9- فَأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْأَلْنني عن بما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they came to not ask me about [عن] about-what [بما] was with him …)
This is supported by what Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: «أياً مَنْ تَدْعُوا». It was said: «مَنْ» may be redundant according to the view of al-Kisāʾī, as he said regarding his words:
31 - 0- يا شاةَ مَنْ قنَصَ لِمَنْ حَلَّتْ له ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O what a doe [مَن] of game, for one to whom she is lawful …)
And it may be conditional, the two being combined for emphasis as stated above. «تَدْعُوا» here may be from duʿāʾ, which is calling, and so take one object; or it may mean naming, and so take two objects — the first by itself and the second by a preposition, after which the preposition is treated loosely and omitted, as in his words:
312 - 1- دَعَتْني أخاها أمُّ عمروٍ. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Umm ʿAmr called me her brother …)
The implied form is: "Say: call your object of worship by 'Allah' or by 'al-Raḥmān'/ — by whichever of the two names you name Him." Among those who held that it means «سَمَّى» (to name) is al-Zamakhsharī.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] paused on «أيّا», changing the tanwīn into an alif, and did not pause on «ما», to make clear the separateness of «أيَّ» from «ما». The others paused on «ما» because of its blending with «أيّ»; for this reason it separates «أيّ» from what it is annexed to in the words of Allah the Exalted {أَيَّمَا الأجلين} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 28]. It is said: «ما» is conditional for those who pause on «أياً» and make the meaning "whichever of the two names you call Him by, it is permissible", then begin anew: {مَّا تَدْعُواْ فَلَهُ الأسمآء الحسنى}; meaning that «ما» is a second condition and «فله الأسماءُ» its apodosis, the apodosis of the first being implied. This is rejected: because «ما» is not applied to individuals among rational beings; because the condition requires generality, which is not valid here; and because it involves omitting both the protasis and the apodosis together.
[Translator's note: the verse number «31 - 0» is given as it appears in the source; the running sequence would be 312 - 0.]

semin-durr:111-111.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {مَّنَ الذل}: there are three views on it. First: that it is an adjective of «وليّ», the implied form being "a protector from among the people of abasement", meaning the Jews and the Christians, because they are the most abased of people. Second: that it is partitive. Third: that it is causal, i.e. "because of abasement". Al-Zamakhsharī inclined towards these two meanings, for he said: "A protector from abasement: a helper from abasement, who keeps Him from it, so that He gains strength through him; or: He has not taken anyone as an ally because of a humiliation befalling Him, to ward it off by his alliance."
The difference between al-dhull and al-dhill was given at the beginning of this sūra.
Al-mukhāfata is speaking in secret such that the speech is not heard. "I struck him until he went quiet (خَفَتَ)", i.e. no sound was heard from him.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» is accusative as the object of «أَهْلكنا»; {مِنَ القرون} is a tamyīz (specification) for «كم»; and {مِن بَعْدِ نُوحٍ}: «مِنْ» denotes the beginning of the range, whereas the first one is explanatory (lil-bayān), which is why what they are attached to is one and the same. Al-Ḥawfī said: "The second is a substitute (badal) for the first." That is not so, because their meanings differ. As for the bāʾ after «كَفَى», the discussion of it has already preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This bāʾ is only brought in a place of praise or blame." The bāʾ in «بذنوب» is attached to «خبيراً», while al-Ḥawfī attached it to «كَفَى». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That is an error (wahm)." I say: He regarded it as an error only because [«كَفَى»] is not made transitive by the bāʾ, and the meaning does not suit it.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّن كَانَ}: «مَنْ» is conditional (sharṭiyya), «عَجََّلْنا» is its apodosis (jawāb), «ما يشاء» is its object (mafʿūl), and «لِمَنْ نريدُ» is a badal baʿḍ min kull (partial substitute) for the pronoun in «له», by repeating the governing element; and the implied form of «لِمَنْ نريد» is: "for whom We wish to hasten it for him."
His saying: {ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ}: «جَعَلَ» here is taṣyīriyya (meaning "to make into/cause to become").
His saying: «يَصْلاها»: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the pronoun in «له» or from «جهنَّم»; and «مَذْمُوماً» is a ḥāl from the agent of «يَصْلاها». It is said that there is an omission in the sentence, namely the omission of the counterpart (al-muqābil), since the original is: "Whoever wants the immediate [life] and strives for it its [due] striving, while being a disbeliever," as indicated by what follows it. It is also said: rather, the original is: "Whoever wants the immediate [life] through his deeds for the Hereafter, like the hypocrite."

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَعْيَهَا}: there are two possibilities. The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because the meaning is "and he did for it its deed." The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and «لها» means "for its sake."
His saying {وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ}: this clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «سعى».

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كُلاًّ نُّمِدُّ هؤلاء}: «كُلاًّ» is accusative by «نُمِدُّ», «هؤلاء» is a badal (substitute), and the second «وهؤلاء» is conjoined to it; that is: "each group We supply, these who strive for the immediate [life] and these who strive for the Hereafter." This is a good implied form. Al-Zamakhsharī, in his implied form, said: "each one of the two groups We supply." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Al-Zamakhsharī implied it thus, and they parsed «هؤلاء» as a badal of «كُلاًّ»; but it cannot be a badal of «كل» on the implication 'each one,' because it would then be a partial substitute (badal baʿḍ), so the implied form should be 'both groups entirely.'"
And {مِنْ عَطَآءِ} is attached to «نُمِدُّ». «العطاء» is an ism maṣdar (noun of verbal action) standing in the place of the passive participle.
«المَحْظور» means the forbidden, withheld. Its origin is from «الحَظْر», which is gathering a thing in a «حَظيرة» (pen); a «حَظيرة» is what is made of trees and the like in which sheep take shelter; and «المُحْتَظِر» is the one who builds the pen.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا}: «كيف» is accusative, either by likening it to an adverbial (ẓarf), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and it suspends (muʿallaqa) «انظرْ», meaning "reflect" or meaning "look."
His saying: «وأكثر تَفْصيلاً», that is: [greater] than the degrees of this world and than the preferment of this world.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَقْعُدَ}: it may be used in its ordinary sense, so that what follows it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may mean «صار» ("become"), so that it is accusative as a khabar (predicate). To this al-Farrāʾ and al-Zamakhsharī inclined, and they cited as evidence:
304 - 3- (Verse:) لا يُقْنِعُ الجاريةَ الخِضابُ ... ولا الوِشاحان ولا الجِلْبابُ
من دون أن تلتقي الأَرْكابُ ... ويَقْعُدَ الأَيْرُ له لُعابُ
(Gloss: The girl is not satisfied by henna, nor by the two sashes, nor by the cloak, short of the thighs/pubic regions meeting and the penis becoming one that has saliva [i.e. discharge].) That is: "and becomes." The Basrans do not extend this by analogy, but confine it to the proverbial saying: «شَحَذَ شفرتَه حتى قَعَدَتْ كأنها حَرْبَةٌ» ("He sharpened his blade until it became like a spear").

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَلاَّ تعبدوا إِلاَّ إِيَّاهُ}: «أنْ» may be explicative (mufassira), because it comes after something that has the sense of speech, with «لا» prohibitive (nāhiya). It may also be the subjunctive-governing «أنْ», with «لا» negating, i.e. "by [saying] that you not…". It may also be the lightened «أنْ» (mukhaffafa), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with «لا» again prohibitive; and the clause in such a case is problematic, in that a request (ṭalab) occurs as the predicate of this class of particle. Similar to it in this problem are His saying {أَن بُورِكَ مَن فِي النار} [al-Naml: 8] and His saying {أَنَّ غَضَبَ الله عَلَيْهَآ} [al-Nūr: 9], since the latter is a supplication, which is also a request. It may also be the subjunctive-governing «أنْ» with «لا» redundant (zāʾida). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be in the position of the accusative, [that is:] 'your Lord has made obligatory the worship of Him,' with «لا» redundant." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is an error (wahm), because «إلا» enters upon the object of «تَعْبدوا», so it must be a negation or a prohibition."
The majority read «قَضَى» as a past-tense verb. It is said that it is used in its original sense; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "and the pronoun in «تَعْبُدوا» would refer to the believers among people until the Day of Resurrection." It is said it means «أَمَر» (commanded); it is said it means «أَوْحَى» (revealed); it is said it means «حَكَم» (decreed); and it is said it means «أَوْجَبَ» or «أَلْزَمَ» (made obligatory, enjoined).
Some of the sons of Muʿādh ibn Jabal read «وقضاء» as a noun, a maṣdar (verbal noun), nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), with {أَلاَّ تعبدوا} as its khabar (predicate).
His saying: {وبالوالدين إِحْسَاناً}: its like has already preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. Al-Ḥawfī said: "The bāʾ is attached to «قضى»; it may also be attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: 'and He enjoined kindness to the parents'; and «إحساناً» is a maṣdar, that is: 'they shall be kind to the parents with kindness.'"
Al-Wāḥidī said: "The bāʾ belongs to the complement of «الإِحسان» and was placed before it, as you say: 'at Zayd's, so alight'." Al-Zamakhsharī disallowed this reading, saying: "because the object of a maṣdar cannot precede it." I say: What ought to be said is this: if what is meant by this maṣdar is that it can be resolved into a maṣdar particle plus a verb, then the matter is as al-Zamakhsharī stated; but if it is a substitute for the utterance of the verb, then the matter is as al-Wāḥidī said. So permissibility and prohibition depend on these two considerations.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying «وبالوالدَيْن إحساناً» is conjoined to the first «أنْ», i.e. Allah commanded that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to the parents with kindness." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] preferred that «إحساناً» be a maṣdar standing in the place of the verb, that «أنْ» be explicative and «لا» prohibitive. He said: "So he would have conjoined what has the sense of a command to a prohibition, as in His saying:
304 - 4- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يقولون: لا تَهْلِكْ أَسَىً وتَجَمَّلِ
(Gloss: "They say: Do not perish of grief, and bear it with fair composure.")
I say: «أَحْسَنَ» and «أساء» are made transitive both by «إلى» and by the bāʾ. The Exalted said: {وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بي} [Yūsuf: 100], and Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:
304 - 5- أسِيْئي بنا أو أَحْسِنِي لا مَلومةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: "Treat us badly or treat us well; you are not blameworthy…")
It is as if «أَحْسَن» had been made to include the meaning of «لَطُف» (to be gracious), and so it became transitive in the way that verb is.
His saying: {إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ}: The two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يَبْلُغانِّ» with the alif of the dual before the doubled, kasra-vowelled nūn of emphasis, while the rest read it without the alif and with fatḥa on the nūn. As for the first reading, there are several analyses. The first: the alif is the pronoun of the two parents, because they were mentioned earlier; «أَحَدُهما» is a badal (substitute) for it, and «أو كِلاهما» is conjoined to it. Al-Zamakhsharī and others took this view. Some found it problematic, since «أحدُهما» is a badal baʿḍ min kull (partial substitute), not a badal kull min kull (total substitute), because it does not fulfil the meaning of the first; and his saying after that «أو كِلاهما» is conjoined to the badal and so is itself a badal, namely a total substitute, because it is synonymous with the alif of the dual. But it cannot be a substitute for lack of benefit, since what is gained from the alif of the dual is what is gained from «كِلاهما», so the substitute adds nothing to the thing substituted for.
I say: This is the sense of the Shaykh's statement. There is something to consider in it, since someone may say: It is granted that the substitute adds nothing to the thing substituted for, but that does no harm, because it is the nature of emphasis (taʾkīd); and had it added something further not understood from the first, it would be a fresh statement (taʾsīs) and not emphasis. And even granting that, it may be answered with what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, for after mentioning this analysis he said: "It is a distributive substitute (badal muqassim), like the poet's saying:
304 - 5- وكنت كذي رِجْلَيْنِ رجلٍ صحيحةٍ ... ورِجْلٍ رَمَى فيها الزمانُ فَشَلَّتِ
(Gloss: "I was like one with two legs, one leg sound, and one leg in which Time struck, so it withered.")
Yet the Shaykh took issue with his words and said: "As for his saying 'a distributive substitute, like [the verse] «وكنتُ…»', it is not so, because its condition is conjunction with wāw; moreover its condition is that the thing substituted for not be true of one of its two parts, whereas here it is true of one of its two parts: do you not see that the alif, which is the thing substituted for, is true of one of its two parts, namely «كلاهما»? So it is not of the distributive substitute." And if both conditions are granted to him, what he said follows.
The second: the alif is not a pronoun but a sign of the dual, «أحدُهما» is the agent of the verb before it, and «أو كلاهما» is conjoined to it. This analysis has been rejected, because the condition for a verb to have a dual sign attached to it is that it be predicated of a dual, such as «قاما أخواك», or of things separated by conjunction with wāw specifically (and there is disagreement about even that), such as «قاما زيد وعمرو»; but the sound view is that it is permissible because it is attested by hearsay, as in his saying:
304 - 6- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد أَسْلماه مُبْعَدٌ وحميم
(Gloss: "…and a stranger and a close kinsman both abandoned him.")
whereas here the verb is predicated of «أحدُهما», which is neither a dual nor separated by conjunction with wāw.
The third: it is reported from al-Fārisī that «كلاهما» is tawkīd (emphasis). This must be repaired by an addition: «أحدُهما» is made a partial substitute, a verb that raises a dual pronoun is understood after it, and «كلاهما» falls as emphasis of that pronoun, its implied form being: "or both of them reach." But this involves omitting the emphasized word and retaining the emphasis, which is disputed; al-Khalīl and Sībawayh permitted it, as in «مررت بزيدٍ ورأيت أخاك أنفسهما» in the nominative and the accusative: the nominative on the implication "they themselves," and the accusative on the implication "I mean them themselves." But there is something to consider here, in that what is reported from al-Fārisī is that he disallowed omitting the emphasized word while retaining its emphasis; so how is his statement to be derived from a principle he does not permit?
Al-Zamakhsharī explicitly rejected emphasis, saying: "If you say: had it been said «إمَّا يَبْلُغانِّ كلاهما», «كلاهما» would be emphasis and not a substitute, so why do you claim it is a substitute? I say: because it is conjoined to something that cannot be emphasis of the two, so it is brought into its ruling, and it must be like it."
I say: He means that «أحدُهما» cannot serve as emphasis of the dual nor of anything else, so likewise what is conjoined to it, for it is its partner.
Then he said: "If you say: what harm would it do you to make it emphasis, while what it is conjoined to is a substitute, thus conjoining emphasis to a substitute? I say: had emphasis of the dual been intended, it would have said merely «كلاهما»; but when it said «أحدهما أو كلاهما», it was known that emphasis is not intended, so it is a substitute like the first."
The fourth: «كلاهما» is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being "or both of them reach," and «إحداهما» is a partial substitute for the alif of the pronoun. The meaning is: "Whether one of the parents reaches [old age] with you, or both of them reach it."
As for the second reading, it is clear. «إن ما» is the conditional «إنْ» to which «ما» has been added for emphasis, and one of the two close letters is assimilated into the other after being converted to it; this assimilation is obligatory. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the conditional «إنْ» to which «ما» was added to emphasize it, and for that reason the nūn [of emphasis] entered; had «إنْ» stood alone, its entry would not be sound. You do not say «إن تُكْرِمَنَّ زيداً يُكْرِمْكَ», but rather «إمَّا تُكْرِمنَّه»."
What Abū l-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] said, Sībawayh explicitly contradicted. Sībawayh said: "If you wish, you may not insert the nūn, just as, if you wish, you may not bring «ما»." The Shaykh said: "He means with the nūn and without it." There is something to consider in this, because Sībawayh only stated that the nūn of emphasis is not obligatory after «أمَّا», even though Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] held it to be obligatory. And his saying after that, "just as, if you wish, you may not bring «ما»," contains no proof that emphasizing the condition with «إنْ» alone is permissible.
«عندك» is an adverbial (ẓarf) attached to «يَبْلُغَنَّ». «كِلا» is dual in meaning without dispute; they differ only about its being dual in form. The school of the Basrans is that it is singular in form, with the pattern fiʿal like «مِعَى», and its alif is converted from a wāw, as shown by its change to tāʾ in «كِلْتا», the feminine of «كِلا»; this is the well-known view.
It is also said that its alif comes from yāʾ, but that is of no account. The Kufans said, and al-Suhaylī followed them, citing as evidence his saying:
304 - 7- في كلتِ رِجْلَيْها سُلامى واحدَه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: "In each of her two legs there is one bone [sulāmā]…")
where he used its singular form: it is dual in form, and for that reason it is declined with alif in the nominative and with yāʾ in the accusative and genitive; so its alif is an addition to the essence of the word, like the alif of «الزيدان», and its lām is omitted according to al-Suhaylī. No explicit text has come down from the Kufans on this, so it is possible that the matter is as al-Suhaylī said, and possible that it was set down on only two letters, since it is part of their school to allow that in declinable nouns.
Its ruling is that whenever it is annexed to a pronoun it is declined as a dual, and when annexed to an overt noun it is declined as a maqṣūr (noun ending in alif) according to the majority of the Arabs, whereas Banū Kināna decline it as a dual in all cases, saying: «رأيت كِلَيْ اَخَوَيْك» ("I saw both your brothers"). The reason it follows the dual with a pronoun but not with an overt noun is something the time is too short to mention, for I have investigated it in «Sharḥ al-Tasḥīl».
Among its rulings: it is annexed only to a dual in form and meaning, such as «كِلا الرجلين», or in meaning but not form, such as «كِلانا»; and it is not annexed to two things separated by conjunction, such as «كِلا زيد وعمرو», except in poetic necessity, as in his saying:
304 - 8- كِلا السيفِ والسَّاقِ الذي ذهبَتْ به ... على مَهَلٍ باثنين ألقاه صاحبُهْ
(Gloss: "Both the sword and the leg that it took off, at leisure, with two [strokes] — its owner cast it away.")
Likewise it is not annexed to a singular intended as a dual, except in necessity, as in his saying:
304 - 9- إنَّ للخير والشرِّ مَدَى ... وكِلا ذلك وَجْهٌ وقَبَلْ
(Gloss: "Good and evil have a limit, and both of those have a face and a front.")
Most commonly it is matched in agreement, so its predicate and pronoun are singular, such as «كلاهما قائمٌ» and «كلاهما ضربتُه»; and rarely «قائمان» and «ضربتُهما» are permitted, considering its meaning. The poet combined both in his saying:
305 - 0- كلاهما حينَ جَدَّ الجَرْيُ بينهما ... قد أقلعا وكِلا أَنْفَيْهما رابي
(Gloss: "Both of them, when the running between them grew earnest, had desisted, and both their noses were swollen.")
Sometimes consideration of the form is required, such as «كِلانا كفيلُ صاحبِهِ», and sometimes consideration of the meaning is required. It is used as a following emphasis, and sometimes it does not follow but occurs as a mubtadaʾ, a direct object, or a genitive noun. «كلتا» is like «كِلا» in everything mentioned; its tāʾ is a substitute for wāw, its alif is for the feminine, and its pattern is fiʿlā like «ذكرى». Yūnus said: its alif is original and its tāʾ is an addition, and its pattern is fiʿtal.
People have refuted him, and that has a place other than this one. The relative adjective derived from it, according to Sībawayh, is «كِلْوِيّ», like its masculine, and according to Yūnus «كِلْتَوِيّ», so that there be no confusion. This much is enough for these two words.
His saying: «أُفٍّ»: «أُفّ» is an ism fiʿl (verbal noun) of an imperfect verb meaning "I am annoyed." This is rare, for most of this category of verbal nouns are imperatives, fewer are of the past, and fewer still of the imperfect, such as «أُفّ» and «أَوَّه», i.e. "I am in pain," and «وَيْ», i.e. "I marvel." By right it ought to be declined, since it occupies the place of a declinable word. There are many dialectal forms of it, which al-Rummānī brought to thirty-nine, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned one expression which completed the forty. They are twenty-two with the hamza vowelled by ḍamma: أُفُّ, أُفَّ, أُفِّ, with tashdīd, with and without tanwīn; أُفُ, أُفَ, أُفِ, lightened, with and without tanwīn; أُفْ with sukūn and lightening; أُفّْ with sukūn and tashdīd; أُفُّه, أَفَّه, أُفِّه; أفَّا without imāla, with pure imāla, and with intermediate imāla; أُفُّو and أُفِّي with wāw and yāʾ; and eleven with the hamza vowelled by kasra: إفَّ, إفِّ with tashdīd, with and without tanwīn; إفُ, إفَ, إفِ lightened, with and without tanwīn; إفَّا with imāla.
And six with the hamza vowelled by fatḥa: أَفَّ, أَفِّ with tashdīd, with and without tanwīn; أَفْ with sukūn; أفا with alif. These are thirty-nine dialectal forms, and the completion of the forty is «أَفاهْ» with the hāʾ of pause. To derive them without this system that I have mentioned is laborious and wearisome, requiring much searching through the books of language and the speech of its people. The Shaykh did no more than say, "We list them vocalized as we have seen them," and then listed them; but the copyists differed from him in vocalizing them, whence the defect arose in it, so I turned to this system mentioned, and praise be to Allah.
Of these dialectal forms seven have been recited: three in the mutawātir (widely transmitted) readings and four in the shādhdh (irregular) ones. Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read it with kasra and tanwīn; Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir with fatḥa and without tanwīn; and the rest with kasra without tanwīn; and there is no disagreement among them about doubling the fāʾ. Nāfiʿ in one transmission read «أُفٌ» with ḍamma and tanwīn; Abū l-Sammāl with ḍamma without tanwīn; Zayd ibn ʿAlī with fatḥa and tanwīn; and Ibn ʿAbbās read «أفْ» with sukūn.
And His saying: {وَلاَ تَنْهَرْهُمَا}, i.e. do not rebuke them; «النَّهْر» is rebuking with shouting and harshness, and its origin is "appearing/becoming manifest," from which comes «النَّهْر» (the river) because of its being manifest. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«النَّهْي», «النَّهْر» and «النَّهْم» are sisters."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {جَنَاحَ الذل}: this is an eloquent metaphor (istiʿāra). It is said that when a bird wants to fly it spreads its two wings and raises them to rise, and when it wants to leave off flying it lowers its wings; so the lowering of the wing is made a figurative expression (kināya) for humility and gentleness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of 'the wing of humility'? I say: there are two possibilities. The first: the meaning is 'lower your wing to them,' as He said, 'and lower your wing to the believers'; so he annexed it to «الذُّل» or «الذِّل», as Ḥātim is annexed to generosity, in the sense: 'lower to them your humble or docile wing.' The second: that you make for his humility («ذُلّه» or «ذِلّه») a lowered wing, as Labīd made for the north wind a hand and for the cold a rein, in his saying:
305 - 1- وغداةِ ريحٍ قد كَشَفْتُ وقَرَّةٍ ... إذ أصبحَتْ بيدِ الشَمال؟ ِ زِمامُها
(Gloss: "Many a morning of wind and bitter cold I have dispelled, when its rein had come to rest in the hand of the north wind.")
as an exaggeration in humbling oneself and showing humility to them." End of quotation. He means that he expressed gentleness by "humility," then borrowed for it a wing, then reinforced (rashsha·ha) this metaphor by commanding him to lower the wing.
Among the charming things related: when Abū Tammām composed his saying:
305 - 2- لا تَسْقِني ماءَ المَلام فإنني ... صَبٌّ قد اسْتَعْذَبْتَ ماء بكائي
(Gloss: "Do not give me the water of reproach to drink, for I am a lover, and you have found sweet the water of my weeping.")
a man came to him with a bowl and said to him: "Give me some of the water of reproach." He said: "Not until you bring me a feather from the wing of humility" — meaning that this is a figurative metaphor just like that one. One of them said:
305 - 3- أراشُوا جَناحِيْ ثم بَلُّوه بالنَّدى ... فلم أَسْتَطِعْ مِنْ أَرْضِهم طَيَرانا
(Gloss: "They fledged my wing with feathers, then wetted it with dew, so I could not fly from their land.")
The majority read «الذُّلِّ» with ḍamma on the dhāl; Ibn ʿAbbās, with others, read it with kasra. It is a metaphor, because «الذِّلّ» (with kasra) is used of beasts of burden, as the opposite of intractability, and so it was borrowed for human beings, just as «الذُّلّ» with ḍamma is the opposite of might.
His saying: {مِنَ الرحمة}: it has four possibilities. The first: it is causal (taʿlīl), so it is attached to «اخفِضْ», i.e. lower [it] out of mercy. The second: it is for explaining the genus (bayān al-jins). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "i.e. this lowering arises from the mercy dwelling within the soul." The third: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَناح». The fourth: it denotes the beginning of the range. His saying: {كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي}: regarding this kāf there are two views. The first: it is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar; al-Ḥawfī implied it as: "show them mercy like their bringing me up," and Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it as: "a mercy like their mercy," as if he took the upbringing to be mercy. The second: it is causal, i.e. "show them mercy because of their bringing me up," as in His saying: {واذكروه كَمَا هَدَاكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 198].

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُبَذِّرْ}: «التَّبْذِيرُ» is scattering; from it comes «البَذْر» (sowing seed), because it is scattered on the ground for planting. He said:
305 - 4- ترائبُ يَسْتَضِيءُ الحَلْيُ فيها ... كجَمْر النارِ بُذِّرَ بالظَّلامِ
(Gloss: "Breastbones in which the jewelry shines like embers of fire scattered in the darkness.")
Then it came to be predominantly used for extravagance in spending.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ابتغآء رَحْمَةٍ}: it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its governor being «تُعْرِضَنَّ»; this is placing the effect in the position of the cause, because the original is: "and if you turn away from them because of your straitened means." Al-Zamakhsharī made it accusative by the apodosis of the condition, i.e. "then say to them a gentle word, seeking mercy." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] objected to him that what follows the fāʾ does not govern what precedes it, as in «إن يَقُمْ زيدٌ عمراً فاضرِبْ»; if you omit the fāʾ it is permitted according to Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī, as in «إنْ يَقُمْ زيدٌ عمراً يَضْرِبْ». If the noun is nominative, as in «إن تَقُمْ زيدٌ يَقُمْ», that is permitted according to Sībawayh on the basis that it is nominative by an implied verb which the overt one after it explains, i.e. «إنْ تَقُمْ يَقُمْ زيدٌ يقمْ». Al-Farrāʾ and his teacher forbade that.
There is something to consider in the objection, because that has been established, by His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9] and the following verse; for «اليتيمَ» and what follows it are accusative by what comes after the fāʾ of the apodosis.
The second: it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تُعْرِضَنَّ».
His saying: «من ربِّك»: it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «رحمةٍ», and it may be attached to «تَرْجُوها», i.e. "you hope for it from your Lord's side," figuratively.
His saying: «تَرْجُوها»: it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «تُعْرِضَنَّ», and it may be an adjective of «رحمةٍ».

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying, the Exalted: {كُلَّ البسط}: accusative as a maṣdar, because it is annexed to it. «فَتَقْعُدَ» is accusative as the response to a prohibition (jawāb al-nahy). «مَلُوماً» is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a khabar (predicate), as has preceded.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خِطْئاً}: Ibn Dhakwān read «خَطَّأً» with fatḥa on the khāʾ and ṭāʾ without madd (lengthening); Ibn Kathīr read it with kasra on the khāʾ and madd, which entails fatḥa on the ṭāʾ [i.e. «خِطاءً»]; and the rest read it with kasra and sukūn on the ṭāʾ.
As for Ibn Dhakwān's reading, al-Zajjāj derived it in two ways. The first: that it is a maṣdar of «أَخطأ يُخْطِىء خَطَأً», i.e. «إخطاءً», when one does not hit [the mark]. The second: that it is a maṣdar of «خَطِئَ يَخْطَأُ خَطَأً», also when one does not hit [the mark], and he cited:
305 - 5- والناسُ يَلْحَوْن الأميرَ إذا هُمُ ... خَطِئوا الصوابَ ولا يُلام المُرْشِدُ
(Gloss: "The people blame the commander when they miss the right course, while the guide is not blamed.")
The meaning on these two analyses is that their killing was not right. Some people considered this reading far-fetched, saying: because «الخطأ» is what is not intended, its meaning is not sound here.
I say: It escaped them that it may mean «أخطأ», or that one says «خَطِئ» when one does not hit the mark.
As for Ibn Kathīr's reading, it is the maṣdar of «خاطَأَ يُخاطِئ خِطاءً», like «قاتَلَ يُقاتِل قِتالاً». Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī] said: "It is the maṣdar of «خاطَأَ يُخاطِئ», even though we have not found «خاطَأَ»; but we have found «تخاطَأَ», which is the reflexive-passive (muṭāwiʿ) of «خاطَأَ», and that indicated it to us. Of it is the poet's saying:
305 - 6- تخاطَأَتِ النَّبْلُ أَحْشاءَه ... وأخَّر يَوْمِي فلم يَعْجَلِ
(Gloss: "The arrows missed his innards, and my day was delayed, so it did not hasten.")
and the other's:
305 - 7- تخاطأَه القَنَّاصُ حتى وَجَدْتُه ... وخُرْطُوْمُه في مَنْقَعِ الماءِ راسِبُ
(Gloss: "The hunter missed him until I found him, with his snout sunk in a pool of water.")
So it is as if those who kill their children are missing the truth and justice."
Some people attacked this reading, so that Abū Jaʿfar said: "I do not know any analysis for this reading," and for that reason Abū Ḥātim declared it a mistake. I say: Others besides the two know it, and praise be to Allah.
As for the reading of the rest, it is good and clear, since it derives from their saying «خَطِئ يَخْطَأُ خِطْئاً», like «أَثِمَ يَأثَمُ إثْماً», when one intends falsehood.
Al-Ḥasan read «خَطاء» with fatḥa on the khāʾ and madd, which is an ism maṣdar of «أَخْطَأَ», like «العَطاء», a noun for «الإِعطاء».
He also read «خَطا» in the shortened form, whose origin is «خَطَأ», like the reading of Ibn Dhakwān, except that he eased the hamza by turning it into alif, which was then dropped, like «عَصا».
Abū Rajāʾ and al-Zuhrī [read] likewise, except that they gave the khāʾ a kasra, like «زِنَى». Both derive from «خَطِئ» in religion and «أَخْطأ» in opinion, and each may be put in place of the other.
Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read «خَطْئَاً» with fatḥa, sukūn and hamza, the maṣdar of «خَطِئ» with kasra.
Ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash read «تُقَتِّلوا» and «خِشْية» with kasra on the khāʾ.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الزنى}: the majority read it shortened (without madd), which is the common dialect; it has also been read with madd, and there are two analyses of it. The first: it is a dialectal variant of the shortened form. The second: it is a maṣdar of «زاني يُزاني», like «قاتل يُقاتل قِتالاً», because it takes place between two. In favor of the madd is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
305 - 8- أبا خالدٍ مَنْ يَزْنِ يُعْرَفْ زِناؤُه ... ومن يَشْرَبِ الخُرْطومَ يُصْبِحْ مُسَكَّراً
(Gloss: "Abū Khālid, whoever commits fornication has his fornication known, and whoever drinks the wine [khurṭūm] ends up drunk.")
and another's saying:
305 - 9- كانت فريضةُ ما تقولُ كما ... كان الزِّناءُ فريضةَ الرَّجْمِ
(Gloss: "What you say was an obligation, just as fornication was an obligation of stoning.")
This is not a matter of poetic necessity, since it is established as a reading in general.
His saying: {وَسَآءَ سَبِيلاً}: its like has preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«سبيلاً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), i.e. 'and its way is evil as a way.'" The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this, saying that, with his statement "accusative as a tamyīz," the agent ought to be a pronoun explained by the tamyīz that follows it, so the implied form «ساء سبيلُه سبيلاً» is not sound, because [the agent] is not a pronoun referring to a generic noun.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: i.e. "except by reason of the right," so it is attached to {لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ}. It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of {لاَ تَقْتُلُواْ} or from its object, or [meaning]: "do not kill, except being accompanied by the right" (masculine plural) or "except [her/it] being accompanied by the right" (feminine). It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a killing accompanied by the right."
His saying: «مَظْلُوماً»: a ḥāl from the nominative subject of «قُتِل».
His saying: {فَلاَ يُسْرِف}: the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] [read] it in the second person, intending the guardian (walī), since the guardian used to kill a group for one person; or [intending] the ruler, returning to addressing him after having mentioned him in the third person.
The rest read it in the third person, which admits what preceded in the second-person reading.
Abū Muslim read it with raised [yāʾ-less] fāʾ-form, as a khabar in the sense of a prohibition, like His saying: {فَلاَ رَفَثَ} [al-Baqara: 197]. It is also said that «في» means the bāʾ, i.e. "by reason of the killing."
His saying: {إِنَّهُ كَانَ}, i.e. "the guardian," or "the ruler," or "the killer," meaning that if he is punished in this world he will be aided in the Hereafter; or [the pronoun refers] to the one killed, or to the blood, or to the right.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ العهد كَانَ مَسْؤُولاً}: there are two analyses. The first: the original involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the one who has the covenant will be questioned about fulfilling his covenant." The second: the pronoun refers back to the covenant, and the questioning is ascribed to it figuratively, like His saying: {وَإِذَا الموءودة سُئِلَتْ} [al-Takwīr: 8].

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بالقسطاس}: the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read it with kasra on the qāf here and in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ; the rest read it with ḍamma in both. They are two well-known dialectal forms, and it is the «قَرَسْطُون» (balance/steelyard). It is also said that it is any balance. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The word is an intensive form from «القِسْط»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it because the two roots differ, then said: "unless one claims the final sīn is an addition, like «قُدْْموس», which is not one of the places where it is added." It is also said with sīn and with ṣād. Some said it is Greek (Rūmī), arabicized.
«المَحْسُور» means the one whose travel has been cut off; «حَسَرْتُ الدابة» means I cut off its travel; «حَسير» means worn out, exhausted, in the sense of «مَحْسُور», and the plural is «حَسْرى». He said:
306 - 0- بها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فأمَّا عِظَامُها ... فبِيْضٌ وأمَّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيْبُ
(Gloss: "There lie the carcasses of the worn-out [beasts]; as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hides, they are hard.")
And «حَسَر عن كذا» means to uncover it, as in the saying:
306 - 1- . . . . . . . . . . . يَحْسِرُ الماءُ تارةً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Gloss: "…the water recedes at times…")
His saying: «تأويلاً»: accusative as a tafsīr (specification). «التأويل» is the point of return, from «آلَ يؤولُ», i.e. best in outcome.
[Translator's note: the entry as given covers more than this verse; the portion on «المَحْسُور» appears to belong to the commentary on verse 29 and the Sūrah's later lexical items, and is translated as written.]

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَقْفُ}: the majority [read] this reading, i.e. "do not follow," from «قفاه يقفوه» when one follows his trail. Al-Nābigha said:
306 - 2- ومثلُ الدُّمى شُمُّ العَرانينِ ساكنٌ ... بهنَّ الحياءُ لا يُشِعْنَ التَّقافيا
(Gloss: "Like statues, high-nosed [noble], modesty dwells in them; they do not spread slander [lit. mutual pursuit].")
And al-Kumayt said:
306 - 3- فلا أَرْمي البريْءَ بغيرِ ذنبٍ ... ولا أَقْفو الحواصِنَ إن قُفِيْنا
(Gloss: "I do not accuse the innocent without a fault, nor do I pursue chaste women even if I am pursued.")
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ولا تَقْفُو» with the wāw retained. It has already been mentioned that retaining the weak letter in the jussive is a dialect of some people, and a poetic necessity according to others, as in his saying:
306 - 4- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... مِنْ هَجْوِ زبَّانَ لم تَهْجُو ولم تَدَعِ
(Gloss: "…of lampooning Zabbān, you did not lampoon, and did not leave off…")
Muʿādh al-Qārī read «ولا تَقُفْ» on the pattern of «تَقُلْ», from «قاف يَقُوف», likewise meaning "follow." There are two views on it. The first: it is transposed from «قفا يَقْفُو». The second, and the more apparent: it is an independent, good dialectal form, like «جَبَذَ» and «جَذَب», because both usages are common; similar to it: «قَعا الفحلُ الناقةَ» and «قاعَها» (the stallion covered the she-camel).
His saying: «والفُؤادَ»: al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿUqaylī read it with fatḥa on the fāʾ and a pure wāw. Its explanation: he changed the hamza into wāw after the ḍamma in the well-known reading, then gave the first letter of the word a fatḥa after the substitution, because it is a dialectal form of «الفؤاد»; one says «فُؤَاد» and «فَآد». Abū Ḥātim rejected it, I mean the reading, and he is excused.
The bāʾ in «به» is attached to what «لك» is attached to; it is not attached to «عِلْم» because that is a maṣdar, except according to those who are lenient regarding the preposition.
His saying: «أولئك» is a pointing to what preceded: hearing, sight and the heart, as in his saying:
306 - 5- ذُمَّ المنازلَ بعد منزلةِ اللَّوَى ... والعيشَ بعد أولئك الأيامِ
(Gloss: "Disparage the abodes after the abode at al-Liwā, and life after those days.")
So «أولئك» is used to point to rational beings and also to other plurals. Ibn ʿAṭiyya offered an excuse for the pointing with it to non-rational things, saying: "He expressed hearing, sight and the heart with «أولئك» because they are senses that perceive, and in this verse they are made to be questioned, which is the state of one who has reason; therefore he expressed them with the referent used for those who have reason. Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding His saying {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4] that He said «رأيتُهم» of the stars only because, when He described them with prostration, which is the act of one who has reason, He expressed them with the referent used for those who have reason. Al-Zajjāj reported that the Arabs express both those who have reason and those who do not with «أولئك», and he and al-Ṭabarī cited:
- ذمَّ المنازلَ بعد منزلة اللَّوى ... والعيشَ بعد أولئكَ الأيامِ
(Gloss: same verse as above.)
As for Abū Isḥāq's report from the language, that is a matter at which one should pause; as for the verse, the transmission in it is «الأقوامِ» ("the peoples"). But there is no need for this excuse, for what you have learned. And as for his statement that the transmission is «الأقوامِ», it is not known; what is known is only «الأيَّام»."
His saying: {كُلُّ أولئك}: a mubtadaʾ, with the clause of «كان» as its khabar. There are two analyses of the noun of «كان»: the first, that it refers back to «كل» according to its form, and likewise the pronoun in «عنه»; «عنه» is attached to «مَسْؤولاً», and «مسؤولاً» is its khabar.
The second: that its noun is a pronoun referring to the one who follows (al-qāfī), and the pronoun in «عنه» refers to «كل»; this is an iltifāt (shift of person), since had it followed what preceded it, it would have been said: "you were questioned about it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«عنه» is in the position of nominative as the agent, i.e. each one was questioned about it; so «مسؤول» is predicated of the preposition and its genitive noun, like «المغضوب» in His saying {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم} [al-Fātiḥa: 7]." End. In his calling the deputy agent (the thing standing in for the unnamed agent) an "agent" there is a departure from the technical terminology.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected his saying, since what stands in the place of the agent has the ruling of the agent, so it does not precede its nominative-governor, like its original. And no one may say: it is permitted according to the Kufans, since they permit the agent to be advanced; for al-Naḥḥās reported consensus on the impermissibility of advancing what stands in the place of the agent when it is a preposition and its genitive noun, so it is not comparable to His saying {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم}. Then what stands in the place of the agent is the latent pronoun referring to «كل» or to the one who follows.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَرَحاً}: the majority [read] with fatḥa on the rāʾ, and there are several analyses. The first: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «مَرِحاً» with kasra on the rāʾ, as indicated by the reading of some, which Yaʿqūb reported, «مَرِحاً» with kasra. The second: there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing exuberance." The third: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
«المَرَحُ» is intensity of joy and gladness. «مَرِح يَمْرَح مَرَحاً» and he is «مَرِحٌ», like «فَرِح يَفْرَح فَرَحاً» and he is «فَرِحٌ».
His saying: «طُوْلاً»: it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «تَبْلُغ» or from its object, or a maṣdar from the meaning of «تَبْلُغ», or a tamyīz (specification), or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). These last two are very weak because they lack meaning.
Abū l-Jarrāḥ read «لن تَخْرُق» with ḍamma on the rāʾ; Abū Ḥātim rejected it and said: "We do not know it as a dialectal form at all."

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَانَ سَيِّئُهُ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read it with ḍamma on the hamza and on the hāʾ, in the masculine, without tanwīn. The rest read it with fatḥa on the hamza and a feminine tāʾ, accusative with tanwīn. In the first reading, «ذلك» points to everything that preceded, including the bad and the good, so he annexed «السَّيِّىء» to the pronoun of what preceded. It is supported by what ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read: «كلُّ ذلك كان سَيِّآته» in the plural, annexed to the pronoun, and Ubayy's reading «خبيثُهُ». The meaning: everything whose mention has preceded, of what you were commanded and forbidden, its bad part, which is specifically what you were forbidden, was a detestable thing. This is the best that can be implied in this place.
As for what some found problematic, that the meaning would become: "everything mentioned was bad," and among everything mentioned is what was commanded, so there would have to be something bad in it, this is a feeble objection, because of the implied meaning I have mentioned.
«مكروهاً» is the khabar of «كان», and the whole discourse is construed according to the form of «كل», therefore the pronoun in «سَيِّئُهُ» is masculine, and the khabar, i.e. «مكروه», too.
As for the reading of the rest, it admits that the pointing by «ذلك» is to the two verbal nouns of the two prohibitions that came shortly before, namely following what one has no knowledge of and walking on the earth exultantly. The second [possibility]: it points to all the prohibitions that preceded. «سَيِّئَةً» is the khabar of «كان», made feminine in line with the meaning of «كُل», then He said «مَكْروهاً» in line with its form.
Al-Zamakhsharī said something fine, namely: "«السيئة» is in the ruling of nouns, in the position of «الذَّنْب» (sin) and «الإِثم» (wrongdoing); the ruling of adjectives has left it, so its being feminine is not considered, and there is no difference between one who reads «سَيِّئة» and one who reads «سَيِّئاً». Do you not see that you say «الزِّنَى سيئة» as you say «السرقةُ سيئةٌ», so you do not distinguish between predicating it of a masculine and a feminine?"
There are four analyses of the accusative of «مكروهاً»: the first: it is a second khabar of «كان», and multiple predicates for it are permitted according to the sound view. The second: it is a badal (substitute) for «سيئة»; this was weakened, since substitution with a derived noun is rare. The third: it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in {عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ}, because it occurs as an adjective of «سَيِّئة». The fourth: it is an adjective (naʿt) of «سيئةٍ», masculine only because the femininity of what it describes is figurative. This has been rejected, in that this is permitted only where [the verb/predicate] is predicated of a figuratively feminine noun; but when it is predicated of its pronoun it is not, as in «الشمسُ طالعةٌ», where «طالعٌ» is not permitted except in poetic necessity, as in his saying:
306 - 6- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا أرض أبقلَ إبقالها
(Gloss: "…nor [is there] a land that has put forth its herbage like its putting forth.")
This is according to those other than Ibn Kaysān; as for Ibn Kaysān, he permits in ordinary speech «الشمسُ طَلَع» and «طالعٌ».
As for ʿAbd Allāh's reading, in it a plural is predicated of with the predication of a singular, since the singular fills its place, as in his saying:
306 - 7- فإمَّا تَرَيْني ولِيْ لِمَّةٌ ... فإنَّ الحوادثَ أَوْدَى بها
(Gloss: "If you see me now, and I have [only] a lock of hair, [know that] the vicissitudes of time have destroyed it.")
Had he said «فإنَّ الحَدَثان» it would have been sound in meaning, but he deviated from it so that the meter be sound.
ʿAbd Allāh also read «كان سَيِّئاتٍ» in the plural without annexation, and it is the khabar of «كان»; this supports the reading of the two Ḥaramī readers [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr] and Abū ʿAmr.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ مِمَّآ أوحى}: [it is] a mubtadaʾ or a khabar, and «ذلك» points to everything that preceded of obligations, of which there are twenty-four kinds, the first being His saying: {لاَّ تَجْعَل مَعَ الله إلها آخَرَ} [al-Isrāʾ: 22], and the last: {وَلاَ تَمْشِ فِي الأرض مَرَحاً} [al-Isrāʾ: 37]. In {مِمَّآ أوحى}, «مِنْ» is partitive, because these are some of what Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet.
His saying: {مِنَ الحكمة}: three analyses are possible. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the returning pronoun of the omitted relative, its implied form being "of that which He revealed, it being part of wisdom," or a ḥāl from the relative noun itself. The second: it is attached to «أَوْحى», and «مِنْ» is either partitive, because that is part of wisdom, or denotes the beginning, or is explanatory; in that case it is attached to an omitted element. The third: it, together with its genitive noun, is a badal (substitute) for {مِمَّآ أوحى}.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَأَصْفَاكُمْ}: the alif of «أَصْفى» is from wāw, because it derives from «صفا يَصْفو»; and it is an interrogative of denial and reproach.
His saying: «واتَّخَذَ»: it may be conjoined to «أَصْفاكم», so that it enters within the scope of the denial; and the wāw may be circumstantial (li-l-ḥāl), with «قد» implied according to some. «اتَّخذ» may be the one that takes two objects. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Its second is omitted, i.e. 'children,' and the first object is «إناثاً»." That is nothing; rather the second object is {مِنَ الملائكة}, advanced before the first, and were it not for that, it would be necessary to begin with an indefinite noun without a justification, because whatever is fit to be a mubtadaʾ is fit to be the first object in this class, and whatever is not, is not. It may also be one that takes a single object, as in His saying: {وَقَالُواْ اتخذ الله وَلَداً} [al-Baqara: 116]; and {مِنَ الملائكة} is attached to «اتَّخذ» or to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from the indefinite noun after it.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا}: the majority [read] with tashdīd on the rāʾ. Regarding the object of «صَرَّفْنا» there are two analyses. The first: it is mentioned, and «في» is redundant in it, i.e. "We have indeed varied this Qurʾān," like His saying: {وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ} [al-Furqān: 50], and like it:
306 - 8- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . يَجْرَحْ في عَراقيبِها نَصْلِيْ
(Gloss: "…my blade wounds their hamstrings.")
and His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذريتي} [al-Aḥqāf: 15], i.e. «يَجْرَحْ عراقيبَها» and «وأَصْلح لي ذريتي». This was rejected, in that «في» is not added redundantly, and what is mentioned is interpreted otherwise; it will come, if Allah the Exalted wills, in [Sūrat] al-Aḥqāf.
The second: it is omitted, its implied form being: "We have indeed varied its parables, its admonitions, its stories, its reports and its commands."
Al-Zamakhsharī said in implying this: "It may be that by «هذا القرآن» is meant the refutation of their ascribing daughters to Allah, because it is among what He varied and whose mention He repeated; the meaning being: 'We have indeed varied the discourse on this meaning, set the variation upon it, and made it a place of repetition.' It may also be that he means by {هذا القرآن} the revelation (al-tanzīl), meaning: 'We have indeed varied it,' i.e. this meaning, in various places of the revelation, so he left out the pronoun because it is known." I say: This implied form that al-Zamakhsharī supplied is the better, because it fits what the verse indicates and why it was brought, for he implied a specific object, either the discourse or the meaning, which is the pronoun he implied in «صَرَّفْناه», unlike the implication of another, who made it general.
It is also said: the meaning is that We did not send it down all at once but in stages; the meaning being "We multiplied the sending of Gabriel to you," so the object is Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Al-Ḥasan read it with the rāʾ lightened; it is said it has the sense of the first reading, since the forms faʿala and faʿʿala may share meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "i.e. We turned the people in it toward guidance."
His saying: «لِيَتَذَّكَّروا»: attached to «صَرَّفْنا». The two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here and in [Sūrat] al-Furqān with sukūn on the dhāl and ḍamma on the kāf, lightened, the imperfect of «ذكر» from «الذِّكر» or «الذُّكر»; the rest read it with fatḥa on the dhāl and the kāf doubled, the original being «يتذكَّروا», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl; it is from reflection and contemplation.
His saying: {وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ}, i.e. the varying; and «نُفوراً» is the second object.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَا يَقُولُونَ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, and there are two analyses. The first: it is attached to what «مع» is attached to, namely the "settling" (istiqrār) [an implied "being"]; so said al-Ḥawfī. The second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a being like your saying"; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ.
Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read «يقولون» with yāʾ (third person), and the rest with tāʾ (second person). Likewise His saying after this, {سُبْحَانَهُ وتعالى عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ} [al-Isrāʾ: 43]: the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it in the second person, and the rest in the third. The sum is that Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read both in the third person; the two companions read both in the second person; and the rest read the first in the third person and the second in the second person.
The basis for the third-person reading in both is that he construed the first with His saying {وَمَا يَزِيدُهُمْ إِلاَّ نُفُوراً} [al-Isrāʾ: 41], and the second likewise. For the second person in both, he construed the first in the sense: "Say to them, O Muḥammad: if there were with Him gods as you say," and the second likewise. For the third person in the first, he construed it with "and it does not increase them," and in the second there is a shift (iltifāt) to addressing them.
His saying: «إذَنْ»: a particle of response and requital. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذن» indicates that what follows it, namely «لابتَغَوا», is a response to the polytheists' statement and a requital for «لو»." Abū ʿAmr assimilated the shīn into the sīn, and the grammarians considered it weak because of the strength of the shīn.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وتعالى}: conjoined to what the maṣdar implies, its implied form being "He is exalted above and is high." «عن» is attached to it, or to «سبحان» by the principle of iʿmāl (assigning the governance), because «عن» was attached to it in His saying {سُبْحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ العزة عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 180]. «عُلُوّاً» is a maṣdar standing in the place of «التعالي», like His saying: {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17], in being a maṣdar not of the verb's own form.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تُسَبِّحُ}: Abū ʿAmr, the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read it with tāʾ, and the rest with yāʾ; both are clear, since the feminine is figurative and also because a separation intervenes.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Then he returned to the heavens and the earth with the pronoun of rational beings, since he attributed to them the act of a rational being, namely glorification." This is built by him on the premise that «هُنَّ» is specific to rational females, which is not as he claimed; this is like his excuse for the pointing with «أولئك» in {كُلُّ أولئك}, which has preceded. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and al-Aʿmash read «سبَّحَتْ» as a past tense with the feminine tāʾ.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّسْتُوراً}: there are two analyses. The first: it is in its ordinary sense, meaning "concealed from the eyes of the disbelievers so that they do not see it." It is also said it is by attribution (nasab), i.e. "possessing a veil," like their saying «مكان مَهُول» and «جاريةٌ مَغْنُوجة», i.e. "a place having terror" and "a girl having coquettishness"; and one does not say of them «هُلْتُ المكانَ» nor «غَنَجْتُ الجارية». It is also said it is a descriptive form for intensity, like their saying «شِعْرٌ شاعِر». This was rejected, in that such usage occurs only with the active participle and from the wording of the first.
The second: it has the sense of an active participle, like their saying «مَشْؤُوم» and «مَيْمون» for «شائِم» and «يامِن»; this is as the active participle comes in the sense of a passive, like «ماء دافِق». This is the view of al-Akhfash, among others.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَحْدَهُ}: there are two analyses. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), though it is definite in form, because it is equivalent to an indefinite, being in the sense of «منفرداً» (alone). Is it a maṣdar, or a noun placed in the position of a maṣdar that is placed in the position of a ḥāl? So «وَحْدَه» is put in the place of «إيحاد», and «إيحاد» in the place of «مَوْحَد», which is Sībawayh's view; or it is a maṣdar with the augmentations dropped, since one says «أَوْحَدَه يُوْحِدُه إيحاداً»; or it is a maṣdar of the triliteral «وَحَد» itself. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وَحَدَ يَحِدُ وَحْداً وحِدَة», like «وَعَد يَعِد وَعْداً وعِدَة»; and «وَحْدَه» belongs to the category of «رَجَع عَوْدَه على بَدْئه» and «افعَلْه جهدَك وطاقتَك», in being a maṣdar filling the place of the ḥāl, its origin being «يَحِدُ وَحْدَه», meaning «واحداً»." I say: You have learned that this is not Sībawayh's view.
The second: it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf); this is the view of Yūnus. Know that this ḥāl in particular, I mean the word «وحده», when it occurs after an agent and an object, as in «ضَرَبَ زيدٌ عمراً وَحْده», is, in Sībawayh's school, a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "making him alone in the striking." Al-Mubarrad's school holds that it may be a ḥāl from the object. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "According to Sībawayh's school the implied form would be: 'when you mention your Lord, declaring Allah's oneness'; and according to al-Mubarrad's school the implied form may be: 'being singled out in the mention.'"
His saying: «نُفوراً»: there are two analyses. The first: it is a maṣdar not of the verb's own form, because «التولِّي» and «النفور» have the same meaning. The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «وَلَّوا», and then it is the plural of «نافر», like «قاعِد» and «قُعود», and «جالس» and «جلوس». The pronoun in «وَلَّوا» apparently refers to the disbelievers. It is also said it refers to the devils, though no mention of them has occurred.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِمَا يَسْتَمِعُونَ}: attached to «أَعْلَمُ». Whatever belongs to the category of knowledge and ignorance, in the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) and in afʿil in wonder, is made transitive by the bāʾ, as in «أنت أعلمُ به» and «ما أعلمك به!!», and «هو أجهلُ به» and «ما أجهلَه به!!»; whereas with verbs other than these two, it is made transitive in both categories by the lām, as in «أنت أَكْسَى للفقراء». «ما» means «الذي» (that which), and it is an expression of disdain and turning away, as if He had said: "We know best the disdain and mockery with which they listen." So said Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
His saying: «به»: there are several analyses. The first: it is a ḥāl, so it is attached to an omitted element. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«به» is in the position of a ḥāl, as [you say]: 'they listen with mockery,' i.e. mocking." The second: it has the sense of the lām, i.e. "with what they listen to." The third: both are in their ordinary sense, i.e. "they listen with their hearts or with the outward of their hearing"; Abū l-Baqāʾ said these two. The fourth: al-Ḥawfī said: "He did not say «يَسْتعونه» nor «يستمعونك», because the aim is not to report listening alone, and it was implied that the listening was by way of mockery, by their saying 'possessed' or 'bewitched'; so the listening came with «به» and «إلى», so that it be known that listening is not intended here as understanding what is heard, apart from this aim." So on this analysis too, the bāʾ is attached to «يستمعون».
His saying: «إذ يستمعون»: there are two analyses. The first: it is governed by «أَعْلَمُ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذ يستمعون» is accusative by «أَعْلَمُ», i.e. 'We know best the time of their listening, with what they listen, and with what they converse in secret, when they are people of secret talk.'" The second: it is accusative by the first «يَستمعون». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The governor in the first «إذ», and in the conjoined clause, is the first «يستمعون»."
