Al-Ḥawfī said: "The first «إذ» is attached to «يستمعون», and likewise {وَإِذْ هُمْ نجوى}, because the meaning is: 'We know best that to which they listen of you, of your recitation and your speech; they listen only for your slip, searching out your fault, and seeking something with which to find fault in you,' meaning in their claim; therefore he mentioned its being made transitive by the bāʾ and by «إلى»."
His saying: «نَجْوى»: it may be a maṣdar, in which case it is the application of a maṣdar to the thing itself for exaggeration, or with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of secret talk," as al-Zamakhsharī said. It may also be the plural of «نَجِيّ», like «قتيل» and «قَتْلَى». So said Abū l-Baqāʾ.
His saying: {إِذْ يَقُولُ}: a badal (substitute) for the first «إذ» according to one of two views; the other view is that it is governed by an implied «اذكُر» ("remember").
His saying: «مَسْحوراً»: apparently it is a passive participle from «السِّحْر» (magic) with kasra on the sīn, i.e. deranged in mind or deceived. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Its meaning is that he has a «سَحْر»," i.e. a lung, meaning that he cannot do without food and drink; so he is a human being like you.
The Arabs say of the coward, "his «سَحْر» is swollen," with fatḥa on the sīn; and of everyone who eats and drinks they say «مَسْحُور» and «مُسْحَر». From the first is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
306 - 9- أرانا مُوْضَعِيْنَ لأمرِ غَيْبٍ ... ونُسْحَرُ بالطعامِ وبالشرَّابِ
(Gloss: "We see ourselves hurrying toward a hidden matter, while we are beguiled with food and drink.")
i.e. we are fed and diverted. From the second is the saying of Labīd:
307 - 0- فإنْ تَسْأَلِينا فيمَ نحنُ فإنَّنا ... عصافيرُ مِنْ هذا الأَنامِ المُسَحَّرِ
(Gloss: "If you ask us what we are about, we are sparrows from among these fed creatures.")
People rejected Abū ʿUbayda's statement as remote in wording and meaning. Ibn Qutayba said: "I do not know what led Abū ʿUbayda to this strained interpretation, despite what the early generations interpreted in clear ways." I say: Moreover, no parable is struck concerning «السَّحْر» that is the lung, unlike «السِّحْر», for they struck parables concerning it; so what follows the verse, His saying "Look how they strike for you parables," fits only «السِّحْر» with kasra.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَإِذَا كُنَّا}: the disagreement of the readers regarding the two interrogatives like this verse has already preceded in Sūrat al-Raʿd, with its verification. The governor of «إذا» is omitted, its implied form being "Shall we be resurrected, or gathered, when we are…", indicated by «لمَبْعوثون»; «مَبْعوثون» itself does not govern it, because what comes after «إنَّ» does not govern what precedes it, and likewise what comes after the interrogative does not govern what precedes it, and both are combined here. On the implication I mentioned, «إذا» is purely adverbial; it may also be conditional, in which case its governor is its apodosis, with the implied form: "When we have become bones and dust, shall we be resurrected or restored," or the like. This omitted element is the apodosis of the condition according to Sībawayh, and that on which the interrogative falls according to Yūnus.
His saying: «ورُفاتاً»: «الرُّفات» is what has been pulverized and crumbled to the extreme; it is a name for the fragments of that crumbled thing. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is dust." This is supported by the repetition in the Qurʾān of "dust and bones." One says «رََفَتَ الشيءَ يَرْفِت» with kasra, i.e. he broke it. The pattern fuʿāl predominates in what is fragmentation, like «الحُطام», «الدُّقاق» and «الفُتات».
His saying: «خَلْقاً»: two analyses are possible. The first: it is a maṣdar from the meaning of the verb and not from its wording, i.e. "we shall be resurrected with a new resurrection." The second: it is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "created."

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذي فَطَرَكُمْ}: there are three analyses. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "He who originated you will bring you back"; this implication has a correspondence between question and answer. The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the one who brings you back is He who originated you." The third: it is the agent of an implied verb, i.e. "He who originated you will bring you back," and for this reason the verb is stated explicitly in its parallel in His saying: {لَيَقُولُنَّ خَلَقَهُنَّ العزيز العليم} [al-Zukhruf: 9].
{أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ} is an adverbial of time governed by «فَطَركم».
His saying: «فسَيُنْغِضُون», i.e. they will move them [their heads] in mockery. One says «أَنْغَضَ رأسَه يُنْغِضها», i.e. he moved it up and down, an «إنغاض», and he is a «مُنْغِضٌ». He said:
307 - 1- أَنَغَضَ نحوي رأسَه وأَقْنَعا ... كأنه يطلُبُ شيئاً أَطْمعا
(Gloss: "He nodded his head toward me and raised it, as if seeking something he coveted.")
And another said:
307 - 2- لَمَّا رَأَتْنِي أَنْغَضَتْ لِي الرَّأْسا ...
(Gloss: "When she saw me, she nodded her head at me…")
Abū l-Haytham said: "When someone is told something and moves his head in denial of it, he has «أَنْغَضَ»." Dhū l-Rumma said:
307 - 3- ظَعائِنُ لم يَسْكُنَّ أَكْنافَ قريةٍ ... بِسِيْفٍ ولم تَنْغُضْ بهنَّ القَنَاطِرُ
(Gloss: "Travelling women who did not dwell in the outskirts of a village by the shore, and for whom the arched bridges were not shaken.")
i.e. were not moved. As for the triliteral «نَغَضَ», «يَنْغَضُ» and «يَنْغُضُ» with fatḥa and ḍamma, it means "moved," and is intransitive; one says «نَغَضَتْ سِنَّه», i.e. his tooth moved, «تَنْغُضُ نَغْضاً ونُغوضاً». He said:
307 - 4- ونَغَضَتْ مِنْ هَرَمٍ أسنانُها ...
(Gloss: "…and her teeth shook from old age.")
His saying: {عسى أَن يَكُونَ}: it may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) verb, its noun being a latent pronoun referring to the resurrection and gathering, which the force of the discourse indicates, or because it is implied in His saying «مَبْعوثون», and «أن يكونَ» is its khabar. It may also be the complete (tāmma) verb predicated of «أنَّ» and what is within its scope, and the noun of «يكونَ» is the pronoun of the resurrection, as preceded.
In «قريباً» there are two analyses. The first: it is the khabar of «كان», and it is an adjective in its ordinary sense. The second: it is an adverbial, i.e. a near time, and «يكون» on this analysis is complete, i.e. "perhaps the return will take place at a near time."

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ}: there are several analyses. The first: it is a badal (substitute) for «قريباً», if we parse «قريباً» as an adverbial of time as preceded. The second: it is accusative by «يَكونَ»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and this is by one who permits the incomplete verb to govern an adverbial; if we make it complete, then it is governed by it according to all. The third: it is accusative by the pronoun of the maṣdar which is the noun of «يكون», i.e. "perhaps the return will be on the day He calls you." Abū l-Baqāʾ disallowed it, saying: "because the pronoun does not govern," meaning according to the Basrans; as for the Kufans, they let the pronoun of the maṣdar govern like its overt form, saying «مروري بزيدٍ حَسَنٌ، وهو بعمروٍ قبيحٌ», and in their view the phrase is attached to «هو» since it is the pronoun of «المرور». They cited Zuhayr's saying on that basis:
307 - 5- وما الحربُ إلا ما عَلِمْتُمْ وذُقْتُمْ ... وما هو عنها بالحديثِ المُرَجَّمِ
(Gloss: "War is only what you know and have tasted; it is not, concerning it, a conjectural report.")
Here «هو» is the pronoun of the maṣdar, and the preposition after it is attached to it; the Basrans interpret it otherwise. The fourth: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "remember the day He calls you." The fifth: it is accusative by the implied «البعث» (resurrection). Abū l-Baqāʾ said these last two.
His saying: «بحَمْدِه»: there are two views. The first: it is a ḥāl, i.e. "you will respond praising," i.e. submissive and obedient. The second: it is attached to «يَدْعوكم»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and there is unease in it.
His saying: {إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ}: «إنْ» is negative, and it suspends (muʿallaqa) the verb of thinking from governing; few mention the negative «إنْ» among the suspending particles of this category. «قليلاً» may be an adjective of time or an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "except a short time," or "except a short stay."

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي}: its like has preceded in [Sūrat] Ibrāhīm.
His saying: {إِنَّ الشيطان يَنزَغُ}: this clause may be parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) between the explained and the explaining, in that His saying {رَّبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِن يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ} occurs as an explanation of His saying {التي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ} and a clarification of it; or it may be not parenthetical but resumptive.
Ṭalḥa read «يَنْزِغ» with kasra on the zāy; they are two dialectal forms, like «يَعرِشون» and «يَعْرُشون», so said al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Had he exemplified it with «يَنْطَح» and «يَنْطِح»" — apparently meaning that the lām of each of them is a guttural letter — "it would not have been to any avail."

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِي السماوات}: regarding this bāʾ there are two views. The more apparent: it is attached to «أَعْلَمُ», as the bāʾ before it is attached to «أَعْلَمُ»; it does not follow from this that His knowledge is restricted to those in the heavens and the earth only. The second: it is attached to an implied «يَعْلَمُ»; so said al-Fārisī, arguing that it follows from that that His knowledge is restricted to those in the heavens and the earth. This is an error (wahm), because mentioning a thing does not entail negating the ruling from what is other than it. This is what the uṣūlīs call "the implication of the proper name" (mafhūm al-laqab), and none held it except Abū Bakr al-Daqqāq with a small group.
His saying: «زَبُورا»: the disagreement of the readers about it has already preceded. He made it indefinite here to indicate partiality, i.e. "a zabūr from the zubur," or "a zabūr in which is the mention of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," so the portion of it is called «زَبور», as a part of the Qurʾān is called [Qurʾān]. It is also possible that «زَبُور» is a proper name, and when «ال» enters upon it, as in His saying: {وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِي الزبور} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 105], it is for hinting at the original sense, like «عبَّاس» and «العبَّاس», «فَضْل» and «الفضل».

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying, the Exalted: {الذين زَعَمْتُم}: the two objects of «الزُّعم» are omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. "you claimed them to be gods." Omitting them for brevity (ikhtiṣār) is permitted; omitting them by restriction (iqtiṣār, i.e. without any implication) is disputed.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أولئك الذين يَدْعُونَ}: «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, and there are two analyses of its khabar. The more apparent: it is the clause «يبتغون», and the relative is an adjective, an explicative, or a substitute; what is meant by the demonstrative is the prophets who were worshipped besides Allah, and what is meant by the wāw is their worshippers, and the pronoun referring back to «الذين» is omitted. The meaning: "Those prophets whom the polytheists call upon to remove their harm, or call upon as gods (so its object or its two objects are omitted), seek…"
It is also possible that what is meant by the wāw is what is meant by «أولئك», i.e. "those prophets who call upon their Lord, or call people to guidance, seek…", so the object of «يَدْعُون» is omitted.
The second: the khabar is the relative itself, and on this «يَبْتَغُون» is a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْعُون», or a substitute for it. The majority read «يَدْعُون» in the third person, and the disagreement has preceded about whether the wāw refers to the prophets or their worshippers. Zayd ibn ʿAlī [read] also in the third person, but built it as passive. Qatāda and Ibn Masʿūd [read] with the tāʾ of address. These two readings strengthen that the wāw refers to the polytheists, not the prophets, in the reading of the majority.
His saying: {أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ}: regarding this «أيُّ» there are two analyses. The first: it is interrogative. The second: it is a relative noun meaning «الذي». The speech of the parsers about it has become abundant only because of the implied forms. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وأيُّهم» is a badal (substitute) for the wāw of «يَبْتغون», and «أيُّ» is a relative, i.e. 'the one who is nearest of them and closest seeks'; or «يَبْتَغُون الوسيلةَ» is made to include the meaning of «يَحْرِصُون» (are keen), as if it were said: 'they are keen as to which of them will be nearest.'" I say: In the first analysis he made it a relative whose ṣila is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, with the mubtadaʾ omitted, being its returning pronoun, and «أَقْرَبُ» as the khabar of «هو»; «أيُّ» then admits being indeclinable (mabniyya), which is most common for it, or declinable (muʿraba), and this has a place more fitting in [Sūrat] Maryam. In the second he made it interrogative, because he made «الابتغاء» include the meaning of something that suspends, namely «يَحْرُصون», so «أيُّهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» its khabar, and the clause is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, because «يَحْرِص» is made transitive by «على». The Exalted said: {إِن تَحْرِصْ على هُدَاهُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 37], {أَحْرَصَ الناس على حَيَاةٍ} [al-Baqara: 96].
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«أيُّهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» is its khabar, and it is interrogative in the position of accusative by «يدْعُونَ»; «أيُّهم» may also mean «الذي», and it is a badal for the pronoun in «يَدْعُوْن»."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "He suspended «يَدْعُون», which is not a verb of the heart; and in the second he separated the ṣila from its object by the circumstantial clause, which does no harm because it is governed by the ṣila." I say: As for «يَدْعُون» not suspending, that is the school of the majority. Yūnus said: it is permissible to suspend verbs absolutely, whether of the heart or otherwise. As for his saying "he separated by the circumstantial clause," meaning by it «يَبْتَغُون», he separated by it between «يَدْعون», which is the ṣila of «الذين», and its object {أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ}, since it is suspended from it, as you have learned; except that the Shaykh had not earlier in his speech parsed «يبتغون» as a ḥāl, but parsed it only as the khabar of the relative; and this is close.
Abū l-Baqāʾ made the relative «أيّ» a substitute for the wāw of «يَدْعُون», and I have not seen anyone agree with him on that; rather all of them make it from the wāw of «يَبْتَغون», which is the apparent view.
Al-Ḥawfī said: "«أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ» is mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the meaning is: they look [to see] which of them is nearer, so they seek means through him; and «أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ» may be a badal for the wāw of «يَبْتغون»." I say: He has implied a suspending verb, namely «ينظرون»; if it is from looking with the eye it is made transitive with «إلى», and if it is from looking in thought it is made transitive with «في»; on both implications the interrogative clause is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, and this is implying what is not needed.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«وأيُّهم» is a mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» its khabar, the implied form being: 'their looking and their concern is [to see] which of them is nearer.' Of it is the saying of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him: 'And the people spent the night discussing which of them would be given it,' i.e. vying as to nearness." The Shaykh said: "He made the omitted «نَظَرُهم ووَكْدُهم», and this is a mubtadaʾ; if you make {أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ} in the position of accusative by «نَظَرُهم», the mubtadaʾ remains without a khabar, so it needs an implied khabar; and if you make {أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ} the khabar, that is not sound, because their looking is not 'which of them is nearer'; and if you make the implied form 'their looking into which of them is nearer', i.e. existent or obtaining, that is not sound, because 'existent' and 'obtaining' are not among what suspends."
I say: So six analyses result in the noble verse, four when «أيّ» is made interrogative. First: it is suspended by «الوسيلة», as al-Zamakhsharī established. Second: it is suspended by «يَدْعُون», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. Third: it is suspended by an implied «يَنْظرون», as al-Ḥawfī said. Fourth: it is suspended by «نَظَرُهُمْ», as Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied. And two when it is made a relative: the first, a badal for the wāw of «يَدْعُون», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said; the second, a badal for the wāw of «يَبْتَغون», as the majority said.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ}: «إن» is negative and «مِنْ» is redundant on the mubtadaʾ to express comprehensiveness of the genus. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is for explaining the genus." There is something to consider in this from two aspects. The first, the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "because the one for explanation must be preceded by some vague item which it explains, as in His saying {مَّا يَفْتَحِ الله لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ} [Fāṭir: 2], and here no vague item has preceded." Then he said: "Perhaps his saying 'for explaining the genus' is a copyist's [error], and he had said 'for comprehensiveness of the genus'; do you not see that he said after that: 'It is said: specificity is meant'?"
The khabar of the mubtadaʾ is the restricted clause of His saying: {إِلاَّ نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوهَا}.
The second: that the condition for that is that it be preceded by something defined with the generic «ال», and that «الذي» can stand in its place, as in His saying: {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30].

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا مَنَعَنَآ أَن نُّرْسِلَ بالآيات إِلاَّ أَن كَذَّبَ}: the first «أنْ» and what is within its scope is in the position of accusative or genitive, according to the two views, because it is by omission of the preposition, i.e. «مِنْ أَنْ نُرسل»; the second and what is within its scope is in the position of nominative as the agent, i.e. "Nothing prevented Us from sending messengers with signs except the denial of the earlier peoples," i.e. had We sent the signs demanded of Quraysh, they would have been destroyed upon their denying, as was the custom of those before them; but Allah knew that some of them would believe and some would deny the one who believes; therefore He did not send the signs, for this benefit.
Abū l-Baqāʾ implied a muḍāf before the agent, saying: "Its implied form is: 'except the destruction of denial,'" as if he meant that denial itself did not prevent that, but what follows upon the denial, which is destruction, prevented it; and there is no need for that, as the meaning stands without it.
His saying: «مُبْصِرَة»: a ḥāl. Zayd ibn ʿAlī raises it with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هي»; it is a figurative predication, since what is meant is the seeing of its people, but since it was the cause of seeing, it was attributed to it. A group read with fatḥa on the ṣād [«مُبْصَرَة»], a passive participle, on a literal predication. Qatāda [read it] with fatḥa on the mīm and ṣād [«مَبْصَرَة»], i.e. "a place of seeing," like his saying, peace be upon him: "The child is a cause of miserliness and cowardice" («مَبْخَلَةٌ مَجْبَنَة»), and like his saying:
307 - 6- . . . . . . . . . ... والكفرُ مَخْبَثَةٌ لنفسِ المُنْعِمِ
(Gloss: "…and ingratitude is a source of vileness in the soul of the benefactor.")
He made these things behave like places, as in «أرضٌ مَسْبَعَة ومَذْأبَة» (a land abounding in beasts of prey and in wolves).
His saying: {إِلاَّ تَخْوِيفاً}: it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and it may be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, either from the agent, i.e. "frightening," or from the object, i.e. "frightened by them."

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والشجرة}: the majority [read] it accusative, as a conjoined item to «الرؤيا», and «الملعونةَ» is an adjective. It is said that it is figurative, since what is meant is "those who eat of it are cursed," because the tree has no fault, and it is the tree of zaqqūm. It is also said that it is literal, and its cursing is its being kept far from Allah's mercy, because it comes forth at the base of Hell. Zayd ibn ʿAlī [read] it nominative as a mubtadaʾ. There are two possibilities for the khabar: the first, it is omitted, i.e. «فتنة» ("a trial"); the second, said by Abū l-Baqāʾ, it is His saying {فِي القرآن}, and that is not so.
His saying: «ونُخَوِّفُهم»: the reading of the majority is with the nūn of grandeur. Al-Aʿmash [read it] with the yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:61-61.t: His saying, the Exalted: {طِيناً}: there are several analyses. The first: it is a ḥāl from «لِمَنْ», so the governor in it is «أَاَسْجُدُ», or from the returning pronoun of this relative, i.e. "You created him [as] clay," so the governor in it is «خَلَقْتَ»; it is permissible for «طين» to occur as a ḥāl, though inert, because it indicates origin, as if he had said: "originating from clay." The second: it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «مِن طين», as He made explicit in the other verse: {وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ} [Ṣād: 76]. The third: it is accusative as a tamyīz (specification); so said al-Zajjāj, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him, but this is not apparent, as no vagueness of an entity or of an attribution has preceded.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرَأَيْتَكَ}: it has been treated fully in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is for address, and «هذا» is the direct object, and the meaning is: 'Tell me about this one whom You have honored above me, i.e. preferred: why have You honored him when I am better than he?' So he abbreviated the discourse." This is close to al-Ḥawfī's statement.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The kāf in «أَرَأَيْتُكَ» is a particle of address with no position in the parsing, and the meaning of «أَرَأَيْتَ» is 'have you reflected' and the like, as if the speaker alerts the addressee so that he gathers himself for what is stated after. Sībawayh said: 'It means «أَخْبِرْني» (tell me),' and he exemplified it with «أَرَأَيْتك زيداً أبو من هو؟» ('Tell me about Zayd: whose father is he?'). Sībawayh's statement is sound where an interrogative follows it, as in his example, but in the verse it is as I said, and is not that which Sībawayh mentioned." I say: What he mentioned is not accepted; rather the verse is like his example, the most one can say being that the second object is omitted, namely the implied interrogative clause, since the discourse is constructed of mubtadaʾ and khabar, as if you said: «هذا الذي كَرَّمْتَه عليَّ لِمَ كرَّمته؟».
Al-Farrāʾ said: "The kāf is in the position of accusative, i.e. «أَرَأَيْتَ نفسَك», like your saying «أَتَدَبَّرْتَ أخرَ أمرِك فإني صانعٌ فيه كذا» ('Have you considered the outcome of your affair? for I shall do such-and-such about it'), and then he began anew: «هذا الذي كرَّمْتَ عليَّ»."
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The second object is omitted, its implied form being 'his preferment' or 'his honoring.'" I say: This is not permissible, because the second object in this category can only be a clause containing an interrogative.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Had someone held that the oath clause is the second object, it would have been good." I say: What rejects that is the requirement that the second object be a clause containing an interrogative. All of this has been established in al-Anʿām, so take it into account here.
His saying: {لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ}: Ibn Kathīr read it retaining the first-person yāʾ in connection and in pause; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retained it in connection and dropped it in pause, which is the rule of those named regarding the yāʾs added beyond the written text; and the rest dropped it in connection and pause. All of this concerns the word in this sūra; as for the one in [Sūrat] al-Munāfiqūn, in His saying {لولا أخرتني} [verse 10], all retained it, because it is retained in the noble written text.
His saying: «لأحْتَنِكَنَّ»: the response to the oath, prepared for by the lām. The meaning of «لأحْتَنِكَنَّ» is "I shall surely take control of them, as one takes control who puts a rope on an animal's jaw (ḥanak) and leads it with it, so it neither balks nor bucks." One says «حَنَك فلانٌ الدابةَ» and «احْتَنَكها», i.e. he did that to it; and «احْتَنَكَ الجرادُ الأرض» means the locusts ate its vegetation. He said:
307 - 7- نَشْكُو إليك سَنَةً قد أَجْحَفَتْ ... جَهْداً إلى جَهْدٍ بنا فأضعفَتْ
واحتنكَتْ أموالَنا وجَلَّفَتْ ...
(Gloss: "We complain to You of a year that has wronged us, adding hardship to hardship, and weakened us, and consumed our wealth and stripped it bare.")
Sībawayh reported: «أحْنَكُ الشاتَيْن», i.e. the one of the two sheep that eats more.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اذهب فَمَن}: it has preceded that the bāʾ [i.e. the letter of «اذهب»] is assimilated into the fāʾ in certain expressions, among them this, according to Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥamza in the transmission of Khallād from him, with disagreement concerning His saying {وَمَن لَّمْ يَتُبْ فأولئك} [al-Ḥujurāt: 11].
His saying: «جزاؤُكم»: the address may be by predominance (taghlīb), because both an absent and an addressee preceded in His saying {فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ}, so the addressee predominated; or the address may be intended for «مَنْ» specifically, in which case it is by way of iltifāt.
His saying: «جَزاءً»: there are several analyses for its accusative. The first: it is accusative as a maṣdar, its governor being the maṣdar before it, and it is a maṣdar clarifying the type of the first maṣdar. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar too, but by an implied verb, i.e. «يُجازَوْن جزاءً». The third: it is a prefatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), like «جاء زيد رجلاً صالحاً». The fourth: it is a tamyīz, which is not comprehensible.
«مَوْفُوراً» is a passive participle from «وَفَرْتُه»; «وَفَرَ» is used transitively, as in Zuhayr's saying:
307 - 8- ومن يَجْعَلِ المعروفَ مِنْ دُوْنِ عِرْضِهِ ... يَفِرْه ومَنْ لا يَتَّقِ الشتم يُشْتَمِ
(Gloss: "Whoever places good deeds before his honor preserves it; and whoever does not guard against abuse is abused.")
and the noble verse is of this. It is also used intransitively; one says «وَفَرَ المالُ» (the wealth was abundant).

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واستفزز}: an imperative clause conjoined to its like, His saying «اذهَبْ». {مَنِ استطعت}: two analyses are possible. The first: it is a relative in the position of accusative as the object of «الاستفزاز», i.e. "incite those of them whom you are able to incite." The second: it is interrogative, accusative in position by «استطعْتَ»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, but it is not apparent, because «اسْتَفْزِزْ» requires it as a direct object, so it is not cut off from it; and were we to make it interrogative it would be suspended from it, yet it is not a verb of the heart, so as to be suspended.
«الاسْتِفْزاز» is making light of; «استفزَّني فلانٌ» means so-and-so made light of me until he deceived me for what he wants. He said:
307 - 9- يُطيع سَفيهَ القوم إذ يستفزُّه ... ويَعْصي حليماً شَيَّبَتْه الهزاهِزُ
(Gloss: "He obeys the fool of the people when he incites him, and disobeys a forbearing man whom turmoils have turned gray.")
From it the calf of a cow is called «فزّاً». The poet said:
308 - 0- كما استغاثَ بسَيْءٍ فَزُّ غَيْطَلَةٍ ... خافَ العيونَ ولم يُنْظَرْ به الحَشَكُ
(Gloss: "…as the calf of a wild cow cried out at a stream, fearing the eyes [of hunters], its udder-milk not yet awaited.")
[Translator's note: this verse is difficult in the source text, and the gloss is tentative.] The original sense of «الفَزّ» is cutting; one says «تَفَزَّز الثوبُ», i.e. the garment was torn to pieces.
His saying: «وأَجْلِبْ», i.e. gather against them hosts from your soldiers. One says «أَجْلَبَ عليه» and «جَلَبَ», i.e. he gathered hosts against him. It is also said «أَجْلَبَ عليه» means he threatened him with evil; and it is said «أَجْلَبَ عليه» means he helped; and «أجلب» means he cried out loudly, from which comes «الجَلَبَة», i.e. clamor.
His saying: «وَرَجِلِك»: Ḥafṣ read it with kasra on the jīm and the rest with sukūn. In Ḥafṣ's reading, «رَجِل» means «رَجُل» with ḍamma, in the sense of «راجل» (pedestrian); one says «رَجِلَ يَرْجَلُ» when one becomes on foot; so it is like «حَذِر» and «حَذُر», «نَدِس» and «نَدُس», and it is a singular intended as a plural. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: it is an adjective; one says «فلان يمشي رَجِلاً» when he is not riding, and of it is the poet's saying:
308 - 1- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . رَجِلاً إلا بأصحابي
I say: He is alluding to the well-known verse, which is:
فما أُقاتلُ عن ديني على فَرَسي ... إلا كذا رَجِلاً إلا بأصحابي
(Gloss: "I do not fight for my religion on my horse, only thus, on foot, except with my companions" [i.e. "neither mounted nor on foot"].) He meant: neither a horseman nor a footman.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the basis that faʿil has the sense of fāʿil, as in «تَعِب» and «تاعب»; its meaning is: 'and your gathering of the footmen'; and its jīm may also take ḍamma, so it is like «حَذُر» and «حَذِر», «نَدُس» and «نَدِس», and other sisters of theirs."
As for the reading of the rest, it admits being a lightening of «رَجِل» with kasra or ḍamma on the jīm; the well-known view is that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for «راجِل», like «رَكْب» and «صَحْب» for «راكِب» and «صاحِب». Al-Akhfash makes this type a true plural.
ʿIkrima read «ورِجالك», the plural of «رَجِل» in the sense of «راجِل», or the plural of «راجِل», like «قائم» and «قيام». It has also been read «ورُجَّالك» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and tashdīd on the jīm, which is a plural of «راجِل», like «ضارِب» and «ضُرَّاب».
The bāʾ in «بخَيْلِك» may be circumstantial, i.e. "accompanied by your cavalry," or it may be redundant, as in the saying:
308 - 2- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَر
(Gloss: "…they do not recite the sūras [lit. 'with the sūras'].")
which has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying: {وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشيطان}: an instance of iltifāt and of placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since had it followed the course of the earlier discourse, it would have said «وما تَعِدُهم» with the second-person tāʾ.
His saying: {إِلاَّ غُرُوراً}: there are several analyses. The first: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and is itself a maṣdar; the original: "except a deceiving promise," so what applies in «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ» applies here, i.e. "except a promise having deception," or for intensity, or "a deceiving promise," the deception being attributed to it figuratively. The second: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "whatever he promises them of false hopes, he promises only for the sake of deception." The third: it is a direct object by extension (ittisāʿ), i.e. "he promises them nothing but deception itself."

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ إِيَّاهُ}: there are two analyses. The first: it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it was not included in what was mentioned, since what is meant by that is their gods besides Allah. The second: it is continuous, because they used to take refuge with their gods and with Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَأَمِنْتُمْ}: an interrogative of reproach and rebuke. Al-Zamakhsharī, by his rule, implied an element to which it is conjoined, i.e. "Did you escape, and so feel secure?"
His saying: {جَانِبَ البر}: there are two analyses, the more apparent being that it is a direct object, like His saying: {فَخَسَفْنَا بِهِ وَبِدَارِهِ الأرض} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 81]. The second: it is accusative as an adverbial. «بكم» may be circumstantial, i.e. "with you," or causal. It is said: his swallowing it up because of them does not necessarily entail their perishing. The answer is that the meaning is "the side of the land in which you are," so their perishing follows from His swallowing it up; and were it not for this implication there would be no benefit in the threat.
His saying: {أَن يَخْسِفَ}, «أو يُرْسِلَ», «أن يُعِيْدَكم», «فَيُرْسِلَ», «فَيُغرْقكم»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read all of these with the nūn of grandeur, and the rest read them with the yāʾ of the third person. The first reading is by way of iltifāt from the third person in His saying {رَّبُّكُمُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 66] to another; the second reading follows the course of the third person mentioned earlier.
His saying: «حاصِباً», i.e. "a pelting wind"; He did not make it feminine, either because it is figuratively [feminine], or by attribution, i.e. "possessing pelting." «الحَصْب» is throwing pebbles, which are small stones. Al-Farazdaq said:
308 - 3- مُسْتَقْبِلين شَمالَ الشامِ تَضْرِبُهم ... حَصْباءُ مثلُ نَدِيْفِ القُطْنِ مَنْثُورِ
(Gloss: "Facing the north wind of Syria, pelted by pebbles like scattered carded cotton.")
«الحاصِب» is also the cloud that throws hail.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْ أَمِنْتُمْ}: it may be the connected «أم» (muttaṣila), i.e. "which of the two matters is the case?"; it may be the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa); and {أَن يُعِيدَكُمْ} is a direct object, like {أَن يَخْسِفَ}.
His saying «تارةً» means "once" and "a turn," so it is a maṣdar, and is pluralized as «تِيَرٍ» and «تاراتٍ». The poet said:
308 - 4- وإنسانُ عيني يَحْسِرُ الماءُ تارةً ... فَيَبْدُ وتارات يَجُمُّ فَيَغْرَقُ
(Gloss: "The pupil of my eye: at times the water recedes from it and it appears, and at times it fills and is submerged.")
Its alif may be from wāw or yāʾ. Al-Rāghib said: "It is, it is said, from «تارَ الجُرْحُ», the wound healed."
His saying: «قاصِفاً»: «القاصِف» may be from the transitive «قَصَفَ»; one says «قَصَفَتِ الريحُ الشجرَ تَقْصِفها قَصْفاً» (the wind broke the trees). Abū Tammām said:
308 - 5- إنَّ الرياحَ إذا ما أَعْصَفتْ قَصَفَتْ ... عَيْدانَ نَجْدٍ ولم يَعْبَأْنَ بالرَّتَمِ
(Gloss: "When the winds blow violently they break the tall palms of Najd and pay no heed to the broom shrubs.")
So the meaning is that it finds nothing but breaks and shatters it. The second: it is from the intransitive «قَصِفَ», i.e. it came to have a crash («قَصِيف»); one says «قَصِفَتِ الريحُ تَقْصَفُ», i.e. it made a sound. {مِّنَ الريح} is an adjective.
His saying: {بِمَا كَفَرْتُمْ}: «ما» may be maṣdarī (verbal-noun forming), and may mean «الذي»; the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of your disbelief," or "because of that which you disbelieved in"; then it was extended, so the bāʾ was dropped and the verb reached the pronoun; this was needed only because the attachment differs.
Abū Jaʿfar and Mujāhid read «فَتُغْرِقَكم» with the tāʾ (the two-dotted tāʾ from above), the verb being predicated of the pronoun of the wind. In the Shaykh's book: "«فتُغْرِقَكم» with the tāʾ of address, predicated of «الريح». Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ [read] with yāʾ of the third person, fatḥa on the ghayn and tashdīd on the rāʾ, making it transitive by doubling, and the reciter (al-muqriʾ) for Abū Jaʿfar likewise, except with the tāʾ of address." I say: This is either an oversight or a corruption by copyists; how can he say "the tāʾ of address" when it is predicated of the pronoun of the wind? It seems he meant "the tāʾ of the feminine," and his pen slipped, or someone else corrupted it for him.
The majority read «الريحِ» in the singular, and Abū Jaʿfar read «الرياح» in the plural.
His saying: {بِهِ تَبِيعاً}: «به» may be attached to «تَجِدوا», or to «تبيع», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «تبيع». «التَّبِيْع» is the one who demands a right, the one who sticks to [the debtor]. Al-Shammākh said:
308 - 6- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما لاذَ الغَريمُ من التَّبيعِ
(Gloss: "…as the debtor takes refuge from the pursuing creditor.")
And another said:
308 - 7- غَدَوْا وغَدَتْ غِزْلانُهم فكأنَّها ... ضوامِنُ مِنْ غُرْمٍ لهنَّ تَبيعُ
(Gloss: "They set out in the morning, and their gazelles set out, as if they were guarantors for a debt, each with a pursuer.")

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying, the Exalted: {كَرَّمْنَا بَنِي آدَمَ}: He made it transitive by doubling; it is from «كَرُم» with ḍamma, like «شَرُف», and what is meant by nobility (karam) is not generosity with wealth.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَوْمَ نَدْعُواْ}: there are several analyses. The first: it is accusative as an adverbial, the governor being «فَضَّلْناهم», i.e. "We preferred them with reward on the day We call." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said in establishing it: "That is because the preference of mankind over the rest of the animals on the Day of Resurrection is clear, since they are the ones charged with obligations, favored, held to account, who have standing. But this is refuted by the fact that the disbelievers on that day are the greatest losers of all animals, because of their saying {ياليتني كُنتُ تُرَاباً} [al-Naba': 40]."
The second: it is accusative as an adverbial, the governor in it being «اذكر»; so said al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. I say: This is an oversight; how can it govern it as an adverbial? Rather it is an object.
The third: it is nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, and it is built only because of its annexation to a verbal clause, with the clause after it as the khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said in establishing it: "It is valid that «يوم» be accusative by construction (building), since it is annexed to something not firmly established, and its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being in the division that comes after it, in His saying {فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ} up to His saying {وَمَن كَانَ}." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His saying 'accusative by construction' should have been 'built on the fatḥa'; and his saying 'since it is annexed to something not firmly established' is not good, because 'firmly established' and 'not firmly established' apply to nouns and not to verbs, and this is annexed to an imperfect verb; and the school of the Basrans is that it is declinable, while the Kufans permit its being built. And his saying 'the khabar is in the division' etc.: the division has no link connecting the clause of the division with the mubtadaʾ." I say: The link is omitted because it is known, i.e. «فَمَنْ أُوتي كتابَه فيه».
The fourth: it is accusative by His saying «ثم لا تجدوا»; so said al-Zajjāj. The fifth: it is accusative by an implied «يُعيدكم», i.e. "He will bring you back on the day We call." The sixth: it is accusative by what {وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ} after it indicates, i.e. "and they will not be wronged on the day We call"; so said Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū l-Baqāʾ. The seventh: it is accusative by what {متى هُوَ} [al-Isrāʾ: 51] indicates. The eighth: it is accusative by what preceded it of His saying, the Exalted: {فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ} [al-Isrāʾ: 52]. The ninth: it is a badal of {يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ} [al-Isrāʾ: 52]. These last two views are very weak because of the many intervening elements. The tenth: it is a direct object with an implied «اذكر»; this, though the easiest of the implications, is more apparent than the preceding, since there is no remoteness in it and not much implying.
The majority read «نَدْعو» with the nūn of grandeur; Mujāhid read «يَدْعُو» with the yāʾ of the third person, i.e. Allah the Exalted or the angel. «كلَّ» is accusative as a direct object on both readings.
Al-Ḥasan read, in what al-Dānī reported from him, «يُدْعَى» as a passive, with «كلُّ» nominative as the deputy agent; and in what others reported from him, «يُدْعَو» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn, followed by a wāw. It has been derived in two ways. The first: the original is «يُدْعَوْن», and the nūn of the nominative was dropped, as it was dropped in his saying, peace be upon him: "You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another," and in the saying:
308 - 8- أَبَيْتُ أَسْرِيْ وتَبِْيْتي تَدْلُكِيْ ... وَجْهَكِ بالعَنْبَرِ والمِسْكِ الذَّكي
(Gloss: "I spend the night journeying while you spend the night rubbing your face with ambergris and fragrant musk.")
and «كلٌّ» is nominative as a badal of the wāw that is a pronoun, or as the agent, with the wāw a mere sign, in the dialect of «يتعاقبون فيكمْ ملائكةٌ» ("angels take turns among you").
The second derivation: the original is «يُدْعَى», as al-Dānī reported from him, except that he turned the alif into a wāw in pause, which is the dialect of some people, who say «هذه أفْعَوْ وعَصَوْ», meaning «أَفْعى» and «عَصا», and then treated the connection like the pause. «كلُّ» is nominative on this only as standing in the place of the agent.
His saying: «بإمامِهم»: the bāʾ may be attached to the calling, i.e. "by the name of their imām," or it may be circumstantial, attached to an omitted element, i.e. "We call them accompanied by their record." «الإمام» is the one who is followed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Among the innovations of exegeses is that «الإمام» is the plural of «أُمّ» (mother), and that people will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their mothers rather than their fathers, and that the wisdom in it is regard for the right of ʿĪsā, showing the nobility of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, and that the children of fornication not be disgraced." He said: "I wish I knew which is the greater innovation: the soundness of its wording or the splendor of its meaning?"
I say: He is excused, because «أُمّ» is not pluralized as «إمام»; this is the statement of one who does not know the craft nor the language of the Arabs. As for the meaning they mentioned, Allah the Exalted called ʿĪsā by his name annexed to his mother in several places, as in {ياعيسى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Māʾida: 110], and reported of him likewise, as in {وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ابن مَرْيَمَ} [al-Ṣaff: 6]; and in that there is a slight upon the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him and honor his face.
His saying: {فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ}: it may be conditional, and it may be relative, with the fāʾ because of its resemblance to a condition. It is construed by form first in His saying {أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ}, so it is singular, and by meaning second in His saying «فأولئك», so it is plural.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن كَانَ فِي هذه}: what is permitted for «مَنْ» is what was permitted for the «مَنْ» before it. The two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr [Shuʿba] applied imāla to «أعمى» in both places in this sūra; Abū ʿAmr applied imāla to the first and not the second; and the rest pronounced both with fatḥa. The imāla is because both are of the yāʾ-type (dhawāt al-yāʾ); the full pronunciation (tafkhīm) is because it is the original. As for Abū ʿAmr, he applied imāla to the first because it is not an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), so its alif is final in form and in implication, and final positions are generally the place of change; as for the second, it is an elative, and for this reason «وأَضَلَّ» is conjoined to it, so its alif is in the ruling of a medial one, because the preposition «مِن» for the one surpassed is as if pronounced, and it is very closely connected to the elative, so it is as if it occurred in the middle, and was protected from change.
I say: This is how al-Fārisī and al-Zamakhsharī established it. It has been rejected, in that they applied imāla in {وَلاَ أدنى مِن ذَلِكَ} [al-Mujādila: 7] despite the explicit «مِن»; so they should the more readily apply imāla to «أَعْمى» with «مِن» implied with it.
As for «أَعْمى» in [Sūrat] Ṭāhā, the two companions and Abū ʿAmr applied imāla to it, but Abū Bakr did not, although he applies it here; it is as if he combined the two matters, being bound by following the transmission. Some distinguished: «أعمى» in Ṭāhā is of blindness of the eyes, and in al-Isrāʾ of blindness of insight; for that reason they interpreted it here as ignorance, so imāla was applied here and not there, for the difference between the two meanings. I say: The question remains, since someone may ask: why was this one singled out for imāla? And had the matter been reversed, the distinction would have stood.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ}: this «إنْ» has the two well-known views: the school of the Basrans is that it is the lightened «إنّ», and the lām is the distinguishing lām (fāriqa) between it and the negative «إنْ», which is why it entered upon a verb of the abrogating class; and the school of the Kufans is that it means the negative «ما», with the lām meaning «إلا». «يَفْتِنُونَك» is made to include the meaning of «يَصْرِفُونك» (they turn you away), which is why it is made transitive with «عن»; its implied form: "they would turn you away by their trial." «لتفترِيَ» is attached to «الفتنة».
His saying: {وَإِذاً لاَّتَّخَذُوكَ}: «إذن» is a particle of response and requital, which is why the conditional particle can occur in its place; «لاتَّخذوك» is the response to an omitted oath, its implied form: "Then, by Allah, they would surely have taken you…"; it is future in meaning, because «إذَنْ» requires futurity, since its meaning is requital. This is like His saying: {وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنَا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرّاً لَّظَلُّواْ} [al-Rūm: 51], i.e. «ليَظَلُّنَّ». And al-Zamakhsharī's saying "i.e. had you followed their wish they would have taken you…" is an interpretation of meaning, not of parsing; he does not intend by it that «لاتَّخذوك» is the response of an omitted «لو», as there is no need for it.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تَرْكَنُ}: the majority [read] with fatḥa on the kāf, the imperfect of «رَكِنَ» with kasra; Qatāda, Ibn Muṣarrif and Ibn Abī Isḥāq [read] «تَرْكُن» with ḍamma, the imperfect of «رَكَنَ» with fatḥa; this is from the intermingling of dialects (tadākhul), and its verification has preceded at the end of [Sūrat] Hūd.
His saying: «شيئاً»: accusative as a maṣdar, its adjective omitted, i.e. "a little inclining."

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying, the Exalted: {ضِعْفَ الحياة}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the reality of this discourse? I say: its origin is 'We would have made you taste the punishment of life and the punishment of death'; for punishment is of two kinds, a punishment in death, which is the punishment of the grave, and a punishment in the life of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the Fire. «الضِّعْف» is used descriptively, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَآتِهِمْ عَذَاباً ضِعْفاً مِّنَ النار} [al-Aʿrāf: 38], meaning a doubled punishment. So the original of the discourse is: 'We would have made you taste a double punishment in life and a double punishment in death'; then the described noun was omitted and the adjective, «الضَّعْف», put in its place, and then the adjective was annexed with the annexation of the described, so it was said «ضِعْفَ الحياة» and «ضِعْفَ المماتِ», as if it had been said «أليمَ الحياةِ» and «أليم الممات»." The discussion of «إذن» and «لأَذَقْناك» is as it was in its parallel.

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذاً لاَّ يَلْبَثُونَ}: the majority read the verb after «إذَنْ» in the nominative with the nūn retained, and it is written so in the copies of the majority. There are three explanations for its being nominative and «إذن» not governing it. [The first:] it stands between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the basis of the two readings? I say: as for the common one, meaning with the verb nominative, the verb is conjoined in it to a verb, and it is nominative because it occurs as the khabar of «كاد», and the khabar of «كاد» takes the place of a noun." I say: So «لا يَلْبِثُون» is conjoined to His saying «لِيَسْتَفِزُّونك».
The second: it stands between an omitted oath and its response, and so is cancelled (ulghiyat) for that reason; the implied form: "and, by Allah, then they would not remain."
The third: it stands between an omitted mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and so is cancelled for that reason; the implied form: "and they would then not remain."
Ubayy read it with the nūn dropped, so its being accusative is by «إذن» according to the majority, and by an implied «أَنْ» after it according to others; in ʿAbd Allāh's codex it is «لا يَلْبَثُوا», with it dropped. The basis for the accusative is that the verb was not made conjoined to what precedes, nor a response, nor a khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As for Ubayy's reading, in it is an independent clause, namely «إذاً لا يَلْبثوا», conjoined to the clause of His saying {وَإِن كَادُواْ لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ}."
ʿAṭāʾ read {لاَّ يَلَبَثُونَ} with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the lām and bāʾ, the bāʾ doubled, passive, from «لَبَّثَه» with tashdīd. Yaʿqūb read it likewise except that he put kasra on the bāʾ, making it active.
His saying: «خِلافَك»: the two companions [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «خِلافَك» with kasra on the khāʾ and an alif after the lām, and the rest read it with fatḥa on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [«خَلْفَك»]. The two readings have one meaning. They cited in this regard:
308 - 9- عَفَتِ الديارُ خِلافَهم فكأنما ... بَسَطَ الشَّواطِبُ بينهنَّ حََصِيْراً
(Gloss: "The abodes were effaced after them, as if the palm-leaf splitters had spread a mat among them.")
And the Exalted said: {خِلاَفَ رَسُولِ الله} [al-Tawba: 81], the meaning being "after his going out." The annexation of «قبل» and «بعد» and the like to the names of entities is frequent, with an omitted muḍāf, so it is implied: from your saying «جاء زيدٌ قبل عمروٍ», i.e. before his coming.
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar or of time, i.e. "a short stay," or "except a short time."
